Understand that glucose-6-phosphate is phosphorylated, which traps it inside the cell.
Recognize that once glucose-6-phosphate is formed, it cannot exit the cell due to the added phosphate group.
Eliminate other options based on their relevance to the first step of glycolysis.

text: Certain plants have leaves in which bundle-sheath cells are tightly packed around veins, which are then surrounded by mesophyll [MEH-zoh-fill] cells. This anatomy is associated with plants that perform what type of photosynthesis?
explainAnswer: Identify the structure of the leaf described in the question.
Recognize that tightly packed bundle-sheath cells are characteristic of C4 plants.
Recall that C4 photosynthesis is an adaptation to efficiently fix carbon in hot, dry environments.
Conclude that the type of photosynthesis associated with this leaf anatomy is C4.

text: Identify all of the following three choices that represent dangers to biodiversity: 1) Allowing fallow farmland to regrow with weeds; 2) Importing an Australian moth to deal with pests on farmland; 3) Relocating mountain lions that have moved into human habitats.
explainAnswer: Evaluate each choice to determine if it poses a risk to biodiversity.
Consider whether allowing fallow farmland to regrow with weeds supports or harms local ecosystems.
Analyze the impact of introducing an invasive species, like an Australian moth, on native species and ecosystems.
Assess the consequences of relocating mountain lions on their population and the ecosystem they inhabit.
Identify that importing the Australian moth represents a direct danger to biodiversity due to its potential to disrupt local ecosystems.

text: What type of neuron is responsible for relaying information between other neurons?
explainAnswer: Identify the different types of neurons: sensory neurons, motor neurons, and interneurons.
Understand that sensory neurons transmit signals from sensory receptors to the central nervous system.
Recognize that motor neurons carry signals from the central nervous system to muscles or glands.
Determine that interneurons connect and relay information between sensory and motor neurons within the central nervous system.
Conclude that the neuron responsible for relaying information between other neurons is the interneuron.

text: Which of the following is definitely known about Australopithecine s?
choices: They were 2 meters tall, on average
explainAnswer: Review the characteristics of Australopithecines based on fossil evidence.
Identify which traits are consistently supported by scientific research.
Eliminate options that are not universally accepted or are exaggerated, such as height and diet.
Confirm that bipedalism (walking upright) is a well-documented trait of Australopithecines.

text: Which of the following genetic disorders is caused by an aneuploidy of the sex chromosomes?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of aneuploidy, which refers to an abnormal number of chromosomes.
Recognize that sex chromosomes are the X and Y chromosomes.
Review the provided options for genetic disorders and determine which is associated with an abnormality in sex chromosomes.
Identify that Turner syndrome is characterized by a missing or incomplete X chromosome, making it an aneuploidy of the sex chromosomes.
Conclude that Turner syndrome is the correct answer based on its association with sex chromosome aneuploidy.

text: Identify all of the following three macromolecules in which sulfhydryl groups can be found: 1) Starches; 2) Proteins; 3) Nucleic acids.
explainAnswer: Understand that sulfhydryl groups are functional groups containing sulfur and hydrogen, represented as -SH.
Recognize that proteins are made up of amino acids, some of which contain sulfhydryl groups in their side chains.
Identify that starches are polysaccharides made of glucose units and do not contain sulfhydryl groups.
Note that nucleic acids, such as DNA and RNA, do not typically have sulfhydryl groups in their structure.
Conclude that only proteins from the given options contain sulfhydryl groups.

text: A scientist has pea plants that are homozygous for purple flowers and plants that are homozygous for white flowers. Given that the purple flower trait is dominant, if the plants are crossed and then the resulting F1 generation is allowed to self-pollinate, what percentage of the resulting F2 plants will have white flowers?
explainAnswer: Identify the genotypes of the parent plants: one is homozygous dominant (PP) for purple flowers and the other is homozygous recessive (pp) for white flowers.
Determine the genotype of the F1 generation by crossing the parents: all F1 offspring will be heterozygous (Pp) and display the dominant purple flower trait.
Allow the F1 generation (Pp) to self-pollinate, which will result in a Punnett square with the combinations: PP, Pp, Pp, and pp.
Calculate the phenotypic ratio from the Punnett square: 3 purple (PP and Pp) to 1 white (pp).
Determine the percentage of F2 plants that will have white flowers: 1 out of 4 total plants is white, which is 25%.

text: Genes can be inserted into plasmids by treating both the gene and the plasmid with a restriction enzyme. The DNA fragments are then mixed and treated with what enzyme to complete the insertion?
explainAnswer: Identify that restriction enzymes create sticky ends on both the gene and the plasmid.
Mix the gene and plasmid together to allow complementary sticky ends to pair.
Recognize that DNA ligase is the enzyme that will seal the nicks in the sugar-phosphate backbone.
Conclude that DNA ligase is necessary to complete the insertion of the gene into the plasmid.

text: Chromatin [CROW-mah-tin] is a complex structure consisting of DNA wrapped around what proteins?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of chromatin.
Recall that chromatin is made of DNA and proteins.
Recognize that the specific proteins associated with DNA in chromatin are histones.
Conclude that histones are the proteins that DNA wraps around to form chromatin.

text: Which of the following hormones promotes bud formation?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of each hormone listed in the choices.
Recall that cytokinins are known to promote cell division and bud formation in plants.
Eliminate the other hormones based on their primary functions: ethylene promotes fruit ripening, abscisic acid is involved in stress responses, and oligosaccharins are signaling molecules.
Conclude that cytokinins is the correct answer as it specifically promotes bud formation.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true regarding tendrils in plants: 1) They can only be found in dicot vines; 2) They can be modified stems, leaves, or flower stalks; 3) They are primarily used for climbing.
explainAnswer: Evaluate each statement individually to determine its accuracy.
For statement 1, recognize that tendrils can be found in both dicots and monocots, making it false.
For statement 2, confirm that tendrils can indeed be modified stems, leaves, or flower stalks, making it true.
For statement 3, acknowledge that tendrils are primarily used for climbing, which makes it true.
Conclude that the true statements are 2 and 3.

text: Which of the following statements about the Calvin cycle is NOT true?
choices: It is an important step during photosynthesis
During the Calvin cycle, the simple inorganic molecule of carbon dioxide is used to make a complex organic molecule
The compound that begins the Calvin cycle is glyceraldehydes [glis-uh-RAL-duh-hyd]-3 - phosphate
The energy needed for the Calvin cycle is provided by the light reaction
explainAnswer: Identify the key components of the Calvin cycle and its role in photosynthesis.
Review each statement to determine its accuracy based on the established knowledge of the Calvin cycle.
Recognize that the Calvin cycle begins with ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP), not glyceraldehydes-3-phosphate.
Conclude which statement is false based on the correct starting compound of the Calvin cycle.

text: A nonsense mutation occurs when a codon coding for an amino acid is changed to what type of codon?
explainAnswer: Understand that a nonsense mutation alters a codon to produce a premature stop signal.
Identify that codons are sequences of three nucleotides that correspond to specific amino acids or stop signals.
Recognize that a stop codon signals the termination of protein synthesis.
Conclude that a nonsense mutation specifically changes an amino acid-coding codon to a stop codon.

text: Which of the following best describes why a complete lack of cholesterol is dangerous for cells?
choices: Cholesterol is necessary for all signal transduction
Cholesterol is required for ATP production
explainAnswer: Identify the role of cholesterol in cellular structures.
Evaluate each choice to determine its relevance to cell function.
Recognize that membrane fluidity is crucial for cell integrity and function.
Select the option that directly relates to the importance of cholesterol in maintaining membrane fluidity.

text: Chlorosis in plant leaves can be caused by a deficiency in what metal ion, which is chelated by the organic portion of chlorophyll?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of metal ions in chlorophyll structure.
Recall that chlorophyll is essential for photosynthesis and contains a central metal ion.
Determine which metal ions are commonly associated with chlorophyll.
Recognize that magnesium is a key component of chlorophyll and is essential for its function.
Conclude that a deficiency in magnesium can lead to chlorosis in plant leaves.

text: Hundreds of fossils of an extinct quail species are found on a small Pacific island. The fossil femur is longer than that of modern quails from the mainland, and the fossil ulna is shorter. Why might these differences exist between the extinct quail and modern specimens?
choices: The extinct quail was adapted to jumping higher because of a higher concentration of predators on islands
The extinct quail was likely evolving flightlessness
The extinct quail fossils were from juveniles
The extinct quail was a hybrid between the mainland species and another, so far undiscovered, island species
explainAnswer: Consider the ecological differences between island and mainland species.
Evaluate the implications of longer femurs and shorter ulnae on the quail's ability to fly.
Analyze the concept of island evolution, particularly the trend towards flightlessness in birds.
Eliminate other choices that do not directly relate to adaptations for flight or lack thereof.
Conclude that the differences suggest an evolutionary trend towards flightlessness in the extinct quail.

text: What is the ecological term for the rate at which a population of a given species will increase when there are no environmental constraints on the rate of growth?
explainAnswer: Identify the key concept related to population growth in ecology.
Understand that biotic potential refers to the maximum reproductive capacity of a species under ideal conditions.
Recognize that this term is used when there are no limiting factors affecting growth.
Conclude that the correct answer is the term that describes this maximum growth rate, which is biotic potential.

text: The selective loss of dopaminergic [dope-ah-min-UR-jik] neurons in the substantia nigra [NYE-grah] is characteristic of what neurodegenerative disease?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question, such as 'dopaminergic neurons' and 'substantia nigra'.
Recall the functions of the substantia nigra and its relation to dopamine production.
Consider common neurodegenerative diseases associated with the loss of dopaminergic neurons.
Match the symptoms and characteristics of these diseases to find the correct one.
Conclude that the disease associated with this specific neuronal loss is Parkinson's disease.

text: Rank the following three ecosystems in increasing order of net primary productivity per unit area: 1) Savanna; 2) Open ocean; 3) Tropical rain forest.
explainAnswer: Understand that net primary productivity (NPP) measures the rate at which plants in an ecosystem produce usable energy through photosynthesis.
Recognize that tropical rain forests have the highest NPP due to their dense vegetation and favorable climate.
Identify that savannas have a moderate NPP, as they support grasses and scattered trees but are less productive than tropical rain forests.
Acknowledge that open oceans have the lowest NPP per unit area because, despite their vast size, they have lower nutrient availability compared to terrestrial ecosystems.
Rank the ecosystems based on their NPP: open ocean (lowest), savanna (moderate), and tropical rain forest (highest).

text: What is the term for mobile elements of DNA that can cut and paste themselves into new locations?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of mobile elements of DNA.
Consider the process by which these elements move within the genome.
Recall the specific terminology used to describe these types of DNA elements.
Match the characteristics and process with the correct term.

text: Pneumatophores [new-MAT-ah-forz] and beets are modified versions of what plant organ?
explainAnswer: Identify the terms 'pneumatophores' and 'beets' as they relate to plant biology.
Recall that both terms refer to specialized structures associated with plants.
Determine the common function of these structures in relation to the plant's needs.
Conclude that both pneumatophores and beets are adaptations of the same basic plant organ.

text: Which of the following statements is true of plant cells, but not animal cells?
choices: They use a cell plate to divide sister cells in cytokinesis
They use channels to allow transfer of ions between cells
They have specialized organelles that likely evolved through endosymbiosis
explainAnswer: Identify the key differences between plant and animal cells.
Recall that plant cells undergo cytokinesis by forming a cell plate.
Eliminate options that apply to both plant and animal cells.
Confirm that the remaining option specifically describes a process unique to plant cells.

text: Identify all of the following three organisms that are deuterostomes [DOO-tur-ah-stomes]: 1) Jellyfish; 2) Humans; 3) Sea cucumbers.
explainAnswer: Understand that deuterostomes are a group of animals characterized by their embryonic development, where the anus forms before the mouth.
Identify the classification of each organism: Jellyfish are cnidarians and are protostomes, while humans and sea cucumbers are both classified as deuterostomes.
Confirm that humans belong to the phylum Chordata and sea cucumbers belong to the phylum Echinodermata, both of which are deuterostomes.
Conclude that the organisms that are deuterostomes from the given list are humans and sea cucumbers.

text: Identify all of the following three structures that are examples of convergent evolution: 1) Whale flippers and human hands; 2) Butterfly wings and bird wings; 3) Spider pedipalps and shrimp antennae.
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of convergent evolution, which occurs when different species develop similar traits independently due to similar environmental pressures.
Analyze each pair of structures to determine if they evolved independently in response to similar functions or environments.
Recognize that butterfly wings and bird wings serve the same function of flight but evolved from different ancestral origins, making them an example of convergent evolution.
Conclude that the other pairs do not represent convergent evolution because they either share a common ancestry or do not serve similar functions.

text: Order the following three types of mature, mammalian blood vessels in increasing mean blood velocity in the systemic circulation: 1) Veins; 2) Capillaries; 3) Arteries.
explainAnswer: Understand that blood velocity varies in different types of blood vessels.
Recognize that capillaries have the largest total cross-sectional area, leading to the slowest blood velocity.
Know that veins have a larger diameter than capillaries, allowing for faster blood flow than capillaries but slower than arteries.
Identify that arteries have the smallest total cross-sectional area and the highest blood velocity due to their muscular walls and high pressure.
Order the vessels based on their mean blood velocity: capillaries (slowest), veins, and arteries (fastest).

text: What plant hormone mediates phototropism?
explainAnswer: Recall the definition of phototropism and its relation to plant growth.
Identify the role of hormones in plant growth and response to light.
Determine which hormone is specifically associated with the bending of plants towards light.
Conclude that the hormone responsible for mediating phototropism is auxin.

text: A patient is demonstrating loss in bone density. Which of the following hormones would be most useful in treating this symptom?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of each hormone in bone metabolism.
Understand that calcitonin helps to lower blood calcium levels and promotes bone formation.
Recognize that parathyroid hormone increases blood calcium levels and bone resorption.
Eliminate hormones that do not primarily affect bone density, such as vasopressin and mineralocorticoids.
Select calcitonin as the hormone that directly aids in treating loss of bone density.

text: The webbed hand of a human embryo develops into five separate fingers by a process of programmed cell death. What is the term for this process?
explainAnswer: Identify the biological process described in the question.
Recall the terms related to cell death and development.
Determine which term specifically refers to programmed cell death.
Confirm that the correct term is apoptosis.

text: Which of the following best demonstrates paracrine [para-krin] signaling?
choices: A tumor cell creates its own growth factors
An allergen results in localized histamine release
The pituitary gland secretes vasopressin [VAY-zoh-pressin] in response to thirst
The pancreas produces insulin after a meal
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of paracrine signaling, which involves the release of signaling molecules that affect nearby cells.
Evaluate each choice to determine if the signaling occurs locally or systemically.
Recognize that the allergen causing localized histamine release affects nearby cells in the immune response.
Eliminate the other options as they involve systemic effects or signaling from a distance rather than local signaling.

text: List the correct order of a secretory protein pathway from synthesis to secretion: 1) Golgi apparatus; 2) Endoplasmic reticulum [reh-TIK-yoo-lum]; 3) Plasma membrane.
explainAnswer: Identify the starting point of secretory protein synthesis, which occurs in the endoplasmic reticulum.
Next, recognize that proteins are then transported to the Golgi apparatus for processing and packaging.
Finally, understand that the proteins are secreted from the Golgi apparatus to the plasma membrane for release outside the cell.

text: The Weddell seal is able to stay underwater for extraordinarily long periods of time due its ability to store twice as much oxygen per kilogram of body mass than humans. This ability is due to the seal having a high concentration of what protein in its muscles?
explainAnswer: Identify the key feature of the Weddell seal mentioned in the question, which is its ability to store oxygen.
Recall that oxygen storage in muscles is primarily facilitated by specific proteins.
Consider the proteins involved in oxygen storage in muscles, particularly in mammals.
Recognize that myoglobin is the protein responsible for storing oxygen in muscle tissues.
Conclude that the high concentration of myoglobin in the seal's muscles allows it to store more oxygen than humans.

text: In the process of peptide synthesis by ribosomes, what specific macromolecule catalyzes the amide bond formation?
explainAnswer: Identify the process of peptide synthesis and the role of ribosomes.
Understand that ribosomes are made up of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.
Recognize that rRNA has catalytic properties in the formation of peptide bonds.
Conclude that the specific macromolecule responsible for catalyzing amide bond formation is RNA.

text: What type of enzyme, produced as part of bacterial immunity against viruses, recognizes palindromic sites on foreign DNA and cleaves them?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which relates to bacterial immunity and enzymes.
Recall the function of enzymes involved in recognizing and cleaving foreign DNA.
Determine the specific type of enzyme that targets palindromic sequences in DNA.
Conclude that the enzyme responsible for this action is a restriction enzyme.

text: Holdfasts, stipes [sty-PEEZ], and blades are characteristic of what group of multicellular algae?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question: holdfasts, stipes, and blades.
Recall the characteristics of different groups of multicellular algae.
Determine which group is known for having holdfasts, stipes, and blades.
Conclude that the group with these characteristics is brown algae.

text: A scientist is separating proteins using size-exclusion chromatography [crow-mah-TAW-grah-fee]. Identify the relative order of elution from earliest to latest of the following proteins from the column: 1) Titin; 2) Myoglobin [MY-oh-glow-bin]; 3) Hemoglobin; 4) Cytochrome [SIGH-tow-krome] c.
explainAnswer: Understand that size-exclusion chromatography separates proteins based on their size, with larger proteins eluting first.
Identify the sizes of the proteins: Titin is the largest, followed by Hemoglobin, Myoglobin, and Cytochrome c, which is the smallest.
List the proteins in order of size from largest to smallest: Titin, Hemoglobin, Myoglobin, Cytochrome c.
Determine the order of elution based on size: the largest (Titin) elutes first, followed by Hemoglobin, then Myoglobin, and finally Cytochrome c.

text: Calcium ions activate muscle contraction because they move what protein from thin filaments?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of calcium ions in muscle contraction.
Understand that calcium ions bind to specific proteins in muscle fibers.
Recognize that tropomyosin is a protein that blocks the binding sites on actin filaments.
Conclude that calcium ions cause tropomyosin to move, allowing muscle contraction to occur.

text: Phosphofructokinase [faws-fo-frook-tow-KYE-nase] catalyzes the formation of what molecule from fructose-6-phosphate?
explainAnswer: Identify the substrate involved in the reaction, which is fructose-6-phosphate.
Recognize that phosphofructokinase is an enzyme that catalyzes a key step in glycolysis.
Recall that the enzyme adds a phosphate group to fructose-6-phosphate.
Determine that the product of this reaction is fructose-1,6-bisphosphate.

text: In order for tropomyosin [troh-poh-MY-oh-sin] to be removed from the myosin-binding sites on actin, troponin [TROH-poh-nin] must bind to what second messenger?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of tropomyosin in muscle contraction, which is to block myosin-binding sites on actin.
Understand that troponin is a regulatory protein that interacts with tropomyosin and actin.
Recognize that the binding of calcium ions to troponin causes a conformational change.
Conclude that this conformational change leads to the removal of tropomyosin from the myosin-binding sites on actin.

text: Cadherins [k uh-deer-ins] are components of what type of cell junction?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of cadherins in cellular structures.
Recall that cadherins are involved in cell adhesion.
Understand that adherens junctions are a specific type of cell junction that relies on cadherins for their formation.
Conclude that cadherins are components of adherens junctions.

text: Identify all of the following three bile components that are secreted by hepatocytes: 1) Bile salts; 2) Bilirubin; 3) Bicarbonate.
explainAnswer: Understand that hepatocytes are liver cells responsible for producing bile components.
Recall that bile salts are derived from cholesterol and are synthesized by hepatocytes.
Recognize that bilirubin is a breakdown product of hemoglobin and is also produced by hepatocytes.
Identify that bicarbonate is primarily secreted by the pancreas, not by hepatocytes, thus it is not a component secreted by them.

text: Which of the following is NOT an example of energy coupling?
choices: An ion releases energy as it travels through an ion channel down its concentration gradient
A kinase hydrolyzes ATP for energy to catalyze a reaction
A transport molecule uses energy from one molecule going down its concentration gradient to power transport of another molecule up its gradient
As protons move down their concentration gradient, ATP synthase gathers energy to catalyze the synthesis of ATP
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of energy coupling, which involves using energy released from one process to drive another process.
Analyze each choice to determine whether it describes a scenario where energy from one reaction is used to power another reaction.
Identify that the first choice describes an ion moving down its concentration gradient without coupling to another process, indicating it does not involve energy coupling.
Conclude that the correct answer is the choice that does not exemplify energy coupling.

text: Polyps and medusae [meh-DOO-see] represent the alternating life cycle forms found in what phylum [FYE-lum] of animals?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question, specifically 'polyps' and 'medusae'.
Recall that these terms are associated with a specific group of animals that have a unique life cycle.
Recognize that the phylum known for these forms is CNIDARIA, which includes jellyfish and corals.
Confirm that CNIDARIA is the correct answer based on your knowledge of animal classifications.

text: Your teacher has a passion for studying human immunoglobulins, but they have to be dimers. What immunoglobulin does your teacher study?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of immunoglobulins and their structures.
Recall that dimers are formed by two identical units.
Determine which immunoglobulin is known to exist as a dimer in its secretory form.
Recognize that IgA is the immunoglobulin that primarily exists as a dimer in mucosal areas.

text: What area of the eye has a high concentration of cones and is so crucial for sharp vision that raptors have two?
explainAnswer: Identify the part of the eye responsible for sharp vision.
Recall that cones are photoreceptor cells that are concentrated in this area.
Consider the unique adaptations of raptors and their vision.
Conclude that the area with a high concentration of cones is the fovea.

text: In prokaryotic [PRO-care-ee-AW-tic] DNA replication, what proteins are responsible for stabilizing the separated strands and preventing them from annealing?
explainAnswer: Recall the process of DNA replication in prokaryotes.
Identify the role of proteins in stabilizing the DNA strands during replication.
Determine which specific proteins are involved in preventing the separated strands from re-annealing.
Conclude that single-strand binding proteins are responsible for this function.

text: In the presence of high amounts of citrate, the reaction catalyzed by the glycolytic enzyme phosphofructokinase [faws-fo-frook-tow-KYE-nase] slows down. Identify all of the following three types of enzyme inhibition that occur in this example: 1) Competitive; 2) Allosteric; 3) Feedback.
explainAnswer: Identify the role of citrate in the glycolytic pathway and its effect on phosphofructokinase activity.
Determine if citrate binds to the active site of the enzyme, which would indicate competitive inhibition.
Evaluate if citrate binds to a site other than the active site, causing a conformational change in the enzyme, indicating allosteric inhibition.
Consider whether citrate is produced as a result of a metabolic pathway that regulates the enzyme's activity, indicating feedback inhibition.
Conclude that citrate causes allosteric and feedback inhibition based on the analysis.

text: What viral reproductive cycle kills the infected host cell while the virus is dividing?
explainAnswer: Identify the different types of viral reproductive cycles: lytic and lysogenic.
Understand that the lytic cycle involves the virus taking over the host cell's machinery to replicate itself.
Recognize that during the lytic cycle, the host cell is ultimately destroyed as new viral particles are released.
Conclude that the cycle that kills the infected host cell while the virus is dividing is the lytic cycle.

text: Which of the following organisms is an example of a bivalve?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of bivalves, which have two hinged shells and are primarily aquatic.
Review the list of organisms provided: Snail, Oyster, Slug, Limpet.
Determine which of these organisms has two shells; in this case, the Oyster fits this description.
Eliminate the other options: Snails and Slugs are gastropods, and Limpets are also not bivalves.
Conclude that the correct answer is Oyster, as it is the only bivalve listed.

text: Proteases catalyze the cleavage of peptide bonds. In most cases, this reaction is carried out through a single nucleophilic amino acid residue in the protease active site. Which of the following could NOT serve as the catalytic amino acid?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of amino acids that can act as nucleophiles in catalytic reactions.
Review the side chains of the given amino acids: Cysteine (thiol), Methionine (thioether), Serine (hydroxyl), and Threonine (hydroxyl).
Determine which amino acids have functional groups that can effectively donate electrons to form a nucleophile.
Conclude that Methionine, with its thioether side chain, lacks the necessary reactivity to serve as a catalytic amino acid.

text: MRSA [mirsa] is an infection-causing bacteria. Which of the following best describes why MRSA is especially difficult to treat relative to many other human pathogens?
choices: It can evade the immune system
It is resistant to many antibiotics
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics of MRSA and compare them to other pathogens.
Evaluate each choice based on how it relates to the treatment of infections.
Determine which characteristic makes MRSA particularly challenging to treat.
Select the answer that best describes MRSA's resistance to treatment.

text: The mechanisms involved in aligning homologous chromosomes in meiosis are also useful for which of the following?
explainAnswer: Understand that homologous chromosomes align during meiosis for proper segregation.
Recognize that this alignment process involves mechanisms that can identify and repair DNA damage.
Identify that double-stranded breaks are a significant type of DNA damage that requires precise repair mechanisms.
Conclude that the mechanisms used for aligning homologous chromosomes can also facilitate the repair of double-stranded breaks.

text: Which animal phylum [FYE-lum] contains the most extant species?
explainAnswer: Identify the major animal phyla and their characteristics.
Research the number of extant species within each phylum.
Compare the number of species across different phyla.
Determine which phylum has the highest number of extant species.
Conclude that the phylum with the most extant species is Arthropoda.

text: In humans, hyperfunctioning of the thyroid gland can result from which of the following conditions?
explainAnswer: Identify the conditions listed in the choices and understand their effects on the body.
Recall that hyperfunctioning of the thyroid gland refers to an overproduction of thyroid hormones.
Recognize that Graves’ disease is an autoimmune disorder specifically known to cause hyperthyroidism.
Eliminate the other options by noting that Cushing's syndrome and Addison's disease primarily affect adrenal function, while cretinism is related to hypothyroidism.
Conclude that Graves’ disease is the correct answer as it directly relates to hyperfunctioning of the thyroid.

text: 5-methylcytosine [methil-SYE-toh-seen] is particularly susceptible to mutations because upon deamination [dee-am-ih-NAY-shun], it becomes what other nucleobase?
explainAnswer: Identify the process of deamination and its effect on nucleobases.
Recognize that 5-methylcytosine is a modified form of cytosine.
Determine what nucleobase 5-methylcytosine converts to after deamination.
Conclude that the deamination of 5-methylcytosine results in thymine.

text: Which of the following would be the most likely explanation for hypothyroidism in a patient whose iodine level is normal?
choices: Disproportionate production of T3 to T4
explainAnswer: Identify the role of TSH in thyroid hormone production.
Consider the implications of normal iodine levels on thyroid function.
Evaluate the options based on their relationship to TSH secretion.
Determine which option directly correlates with decreased thyroid hormone production due to low TSH levels.

text: Some herbivores, such as rabbits and horses, possess the ability to digest cellulose with the aid of bacteria located in a pouch at the beginning of the large intestine. What is the name of this pouch?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question, such as 'herbivores', 'digest cellulose', and 'bacteria'.
Recall the anatomy of herbivores and their digestive systems.
Focus on the specific part of the digestive system mentioned that aids in cellulose digestion.
Recognize that the pouch at the beginning of the large intestine is commonly known as the cecum.

text: What type of population selection would occur in an environment that is very close to its carrying capacity?
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of carrying capacity, which is the maximum population size that an environment can sustain.
Recognize that when a population is near its carrying capacity, resources are limited and competition is high.
Identify that K-selection refers to reproductive strategies that favor the survival of a few offspring with high parental investment.
Differentiate K-selection from r-selection, which occurs in environments with abundant resources and lower competition.

text: Identify all of the following three molecules that are exocrine [EX-oh-krin] products: 1) EGF; 2) Amylase; 3) ADH.
explainAnswer: Understand that exocrine products are substances secreted by glands through ducts to the outside of the body or into the digestive system.

Identify each molecule: EGF (Epidermal Growth Factor) is a hormone that acts locally, ADH (Antidiuretic Hormone) is a hormone that acts on the kidneys, and Amylase is an enzyme that helps in digestion.
Determine which of these molecules is secreted through a duct: Amylase is produced by the salivary glands and secreted into the mouth, making it an exocrine product.
Conclude that the only exocrine product among the three listed is Amylase.

text: In fungal [FUN-gul] reproduction, what stage is characterized by the haploid [HAP-loid] nuclei [NEW-klee-eye] of different parents fusing into a single diploid [DIH-ployd] nucleus?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms related to fungal reproduction.
Understand the definitions of haploid and diploid nuclei.
Recognize that the fusion of haploid nuclei from different parents leads to a diploid stage.
Recall the specific term used to describe this fusion process in fungi.
Conclude that the correct term for this stage is KARYOGAMY.

text: Which of the following is not a behavior generally associated with cancerous cells?
choices: They induce angiogenesis [an-gee-oh-g en-u h-s is]
They cannot proliferate when not adherent to substrate
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics commonly associated with cancerous cells.
Recall that cancerous cells often induce angiogenesis and produce telomerase.
Understand that cancerous cells typically do not stop cell division.
Recognize that normal cells usually require adherence to a substrate to proliferate, while cancerous cells can grow without this requirement.
Conclude that the statement 'They cannot proliferate when not adherent to substrate' is not a behavior associated with cancerous cells.

text: A 19th-century Danish scientist classified bacteria based on the ability of their cell walls to retain crystal violet, which is due to the abundance of what polymer?
explainAnswer: Identify the scientist known for classifying bacteria based on cell wall properties.
Recall the staining technique that involves crystal violet and its relation to bacterial classification.
Determine the key component of bacterial cell walls that affects crystal violet retention.
Conclude that the polymer responsible for this property is peptidoglycan.

text: Which of the following compounds would one use to detect the presence of DNA in an agarose gel?
explainAnswer: Identify the purpose of the compounds listed in the choices.
Recall that Ethidium bromide is a nucleic acid stain that intercalates with DNA.
Consider the other options and their common uses in laboratory settings.
Determine which compound is specifically used for visualizing DNA in agarose gels.

text: SDS is a detergent. Which of the following explains how SDS denatures proteins?
choices: Interferes with the hydrophobic interactions that normally stabilize the proteins
Interferes with the hydrophillic interactions that normally stabilize the proteins
Interferes with the amphiphillic [amfih-FILL-ic] interactions that normally stabilize the proteins
explainAnswer: Understand that SDS is a detergent that disrupts protein structure.
Identify that proteins are stabilized by various interactions, including hydrophobic interactions.
Recognize that hydrophobic interactions occur between nonpolar side chains of amino acids.
Determine that SDS disrupts these hydrophobic interactions, leading to denaturation.
Select the choice that correctly states SDS interferes with hydrophobic interactions.

text: John Gurdon studied totipotency [toh-TIH-pah-ten-see] by implanting a nucleus from a fully-differentiated frog cell into enucleated egg cells. Which of the following best describes what he observed about the egg?
choices: It continued to divide, but stopped development prior to forming a tadpole
It continued to divide and developed into a tadpole as normal
It did not begin to divide after nucleation
It continued to divide, but skipped the tadpole stage and formed a frog
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of totipotency and how it relates to cell differentiation.
Recognize that implanting a nucleus from a differentiated cell into an enucleated egg cell tests the egg's ability to reprogram the nucleus.
Consider the implications of using a fully-differentiated nucleus and how it may affect the developmental potential of the egg.
Evaluate the choices based on the expected outcome of the experiment, focusing on the limitations of the differentiated nucleus.
Select the choice that indicates the egg continued to divide but did not complete normal development.

text: Which of the following is not true regarding mitosis?
choices: Sister chromatids are held together by cohesion [coh-ee-sin] complexes
M-Cdk drives entry of the cell into mitosis
The mitotic spindle is built from actin filaments
The Golgi apparatus becomes less prominent during metaphase
explainAnswer: Identify the key components and processes involved in mitosis.
Evaluate each statement to determine its accuracy based on established biological knowledge.
Recall that the mitotic spindle is primarily composed of microtubules, not actin filaments.
Conclude that the statement about the mitotic spindle is the one that is not true.

text: Which of the following is NOT a biogenic amine?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of biogenic amines and their common characteristics.
List the given options and categorize them based on their biochemical classification.
Determine which of the listed options is a peptide or does not fit the biogenic amine category.
Conclude that Dynorphin is a peptide and not a biogenic amine.

text: What vitamin, essential to humans, is involved in collagen synthesis?
explainAnswer: Identify the vitamins that are known to be essential for human health.
Research the specific functions of these vitamins, focusing on their roles in bodily processes.
Determine which vitamin is specifically linked to collagen synthesis based on your research.
Conclude that Vitamin C is the vitamin involved in collagen synthesis.

text: What nerve is known as the “wandering” nerve, as it travels down into the chest and abdomen from the throat and larynx, where it helps control the cardiovascular and gastrointestinal systems?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of the nerve in question, focusing on its role in the cardiovascular and gastrointestinal systems.
Recall the anatomical path of the nerve, noting that it extends from the throat and larynx down into the chest and abdomen.
Consider the nickname 'wandering' and how it relates to the nerve's extensive distribution throughout the body.
Cross-reference your knowledge of cranial nerves to determine which one fits this description.
Conclude that the nerve in question is the vagus nerve based on its functions and anatomical path.

text: In which of the following organisms would one most likely find nematocysts?
explainAnswer: Identify the defining characteristics of nematocysts, which are specialized cells used for capturing prey and defense.
Review the organisms listed and determine which are known to possess cnidocytes, the cells that contain nematocysts.
Recognize that jellyfish are part of the phylum Cnidaria, which is characterized by the presence of nematocysts.
Eliminate the other options (octopus, sponge, sea cucumber) as they do not have nematocysts.

text: What nucleobase does thymine pair with in DNA?
explainAnswer: Recall the base pairing rules in DNA, which state that specific nucleobases pair with each other.
Identify that thymine (T) is one of the four nucleobases in DNA.
Know that thymine pairs with adenine (A) according to the base pairing rules.
Conclude that the nucleobase thymine pairs with adenine in DNA.

text: What enzyme is the major regulation site of glycolysis [glye-KAWL-eh-sis] ?
explainAnswer: Recall the main metabolic pathways involved in cellular respiration.
Identify the key steps of glycolysis and their associated enzymes.
Determine which enzyme is responsible for the major regulatory step in glycolysis.
Recognize that phosphofructokinase is the enzyme that catalyzes this regulatory step.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of eukaryotic mRNA processing: 1) The 5-prime end is capped with a modified cytosine residue; 2) The 5-prime end is capped in the nucleus; 3) The 3-prime end is adenylated in the cytosol.
explainAnswer: Understand that eukaryotic mRNA processing occurs primarily in the nucleus.
Identify that the 5-prime cap is added to the mRNA in the nucleus, making statement 2 true.
Recognize that the 5-prime cap is not a modified cytosine residue, which makes statement 1 false.
Note that the 3-prime end is adenylated in the nucleus, not the cytosol, making statement 3 false.

text: Which of the following is NOT an example of negative feedback?
choices: High blood glucose causing insulin release
Secretion of cortisol inhibiting ACTH release
Release of platelet activating factor during clotting
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of negative feedback, which is a process that counteracts changes to maintain stability.
Review each choice to determine if it describes a mechanism that reduces or inhibits a process.
Recognize that excess ATP inhibiting phosphofructokinase, insulin release in response to high blood glucose, and cortisol inhibiting ACTH are all examples of negative feedback.
Determine that the release of platelet activating factor during clotting is a positive feedback mechanism that amplifies the response.
Conclude that the correct answer is the choice that does not represent negative feedback.

text: Insulin is secreted by what structures in the pancreas?
answer: ISLETS OF LANGERHANS (ACCEPT: BETA CELLS OF THE ISLETS OF LANGERHANS,
explainAnswer: Identify the main function of the pancreas related to insulin production.
Recall the specific structures within the pancreas responsible for hormone secretion.
Recognize that the Islets of Langerhans are clusters of cells that include beta cells.
Conclude that insulin is secreted by the beta cells located in the Islets of Langerhans.

text: Fish extrude nitrogenous waste in what toxic form?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of nitrogenous waste produced by animals.
Recall that fish primarily excrete waste through their gills and urine.
Determine the form in which ammonia is produced and excreted by aquatic animals.
Conclude that fish excrete nitrogenous waste mainly in the form of ammonia.

text: What two blood-sugar-relevant hormones are secreted by the islets [EYE-lets] of Langerhans [LAYN-gur-honz] ?
explainAnswer: Identify the location of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas.
Recall the function of the islets of Langerhans in regulating blood sugar levels.
List the hormones associated with blood sugar regulation.
Confirm that glucagon and insulin are the primary hormones secreted by the islets.

text: What enzyme, found in the human stomach, is activated by hydrochloric acid and breaks down proteins?
explainAnswer: Identify the location in the human body where protein digestion occurs.
Recall the role of hydrochloric acid in the stomach during digestion.
Determine which enzyme is specifically activated by hydrochloric acid to aid in protein breakdown.
Conclude that the enzyme responsible for breaking down proteins in the stomach is pepsin.

text: What type of phagocytic cell can primarily be found under mucosal [myoo-KOH-sul] surfaces and plays a primary role in responding to multicellular pathogens?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of each type of phagocytic cell mentioned in the choices.
Focus on the specific role of each cell type in relation to mucosal surfaces and multicellular pathogens.
Determine which cell type is primarily associated with responding to multicellular pathogens in mucosal areas.
Select the correct answer based on the identified characteristics of the cell types.

text: Identify all of the following three pathways during which oxidative phosphorylation [faws-four-il-AY-shun] occurs: 1) Photosynthesis; 2) Krebs cycle; 3) Electron transport chain.
explainAnswer: Understand that oxidative phosphorylation is a process that occurs in cellular respiration and is primarily associated with the electron transport chain.
Recognize that photosynthesis involves a different process called photophosphorylation, not oxidative phosphorylation.
Identify that the Krebs cycle produces electron carriers that feed into the electron transport chain but does not itself involve oxidative phosphorylation.
Conclude that the pathways where oxidative phosphorylation occurs are the electron transport chain and not photosynthesis or the Krebs cycle.

text: Identify all of the following three organisms that follow the haplo-diploid system of sex determination: 1) Crows; 2) Ants; 3) Bees.
explainAnswer: Understand that the haplo-diploid system means males are haploid (develop from unfertilized eggs) and females are diploid (develop from fertilized eggs).
Identify that ants and bees reproduce using this system, where males are produced from unfertilized eggs and females from fertilized ones.
Recognize that crows do not follow the haplo-diploid system; they have a typical diploid system of sex determination.

text: What type of meristem is primarily responsible for secondary growth?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of meristems: apical, lateral, and intercalary.
Understand that apical meristems are responsible for primary growth, which increases the length of the plant.
Recognize that lateral meristems, such as the vascular cambium and cork cambium, are responsible for secondary growth, which increases the girth of the plant.
Confirm that lateral meristems are the correct answer for secondary growth.

text: In part of the Hershey-Chase experiment, phages were grown in the presence of a radioactive isotope of what element found in proteins but not in DNA?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of DNA and proteins to determine which elements are present in each.
Recall that DNA contains phosphorus and does not contain sulfur.
Recognize that proteins contain sulfur in the form of amino acids like cysteine and methionine.
Conclude that the radioactive isotope used in the experiment must be sulfur, as it is found in proteins but not in DNA.

text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding short day plants?
choices: Flowering occurs when night length is less than critical length
Continuity of darkness is crucial; flowering will not occur if darkness is interrupted by a momentary light flash
Short day plants are synonymous with long night plants
Photoperiod can be detected via phytochromes
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of short day plants and their flowering requirements.
Review the definitions of critical night length and how it affects flowering.
Analyze each statement to see if it aligns with the known behavior of short day plants.
Determine which statement contradicts the established understanding of short day plants.
Select the statement that is NOT correct based on your analysis.

text: Identify all of the following three choices that are pieces of evidence that lend credence to the endosymbiotic theory: 1) Chloroplasts contain their own genomes; 2) Mitochondria contain bacteria-like ribosomes; 3) All mitochondrial proteins are synthesized in the nucleus.
explainAnswer: Evaluate each choice to determine if it supports the endosymbiotic theory.
Recognize that the endosymbiotic theory suggests that certain organelles originated from free-living prokaryotes.
Identify that chloroplasts having their own genomes supports this theory as it indicates a prokaryotic origin.
Note that mitochondria containing bacteria-like ribosomes also supports the theory due to similarities with prokaryotes.
Conclude that the third choice does not support the theory, as it does not indicate a prokaryotic origin.

text: Which of the following vitamins is NOT fat soluble?
explainAnswer: Identify the categories of vitamins: fat-soluble and water-soluble.
List the fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, and K.
Recognize that Tocopherol (Vitamin E), Phylloquinone (Vitamin K), and Calciferol (Vitamin D) are all fat-soluble.
Determine that Biotin is not included in the fat-soluble vitamins and is instead water-soluble.

text: Which of the following statements is true regarding fungal mutualism?
choices: Most endophytes are basidiomycetes [buh-s id-ee-o h-mye-seets]
Many species of ants culture fungi inside of their bodies
Lichens are capable of nitrogen fixation
Plants can generally grow normally without endophytes
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in each statement related to fungal mutualism.
Evaluate the accuracy of each statement based on known biological facts.
Recall that lichens are symbiotic relationships between fungi and photosynthetic organisms, and some can fix nitrogen.
Determine which statement is true based on the evaluation and recall.

text: Identify all of the following three processes that occur in marine fish, in contrast to freshwater fish: 1) Excretion of salt from the gills; 2) Loss of water from body surfaces due to osmosis; 3) Excretion of large amounts of dilute urine.
explainAnswer: Understand that marine fish are adapted to a salty environment, while freshwater fish are adapted to a less salty environment.
Recognize that marine fish actively excrete salt through their gills to maintain osmotic balance.
Identify that marine fish lose water through osmosis due to the higher salinity of the surrounding water.
Note that freshwater fish do not excrete large amounts of dilute urine, as they need to retain water instead.

text: Which of the following sea turtle species is phylogenetically distinct from the others and can maintain body temperature elevated above ambient levels? Y) Kemp’s Ridley X) Leatherback Y) Green Z) Loggerhead
explainAnswer: Identify the unique characteristics of each sea turtle species listed.
Research the ability of each species to maintain elevated body temperature.
Determine which species is known for being phylogenetically distinct and has the ability to thermoregulate.
Conclude that the Leatherback is the only species that meets both criteria.

text: Cryptonephridia [kripto-neh-FRID-ee-ah] can be found in the excretory systems of which of the following organisms?
explainAnswer: Identify the organisms listed in the choices and their respective excretory systems.
Research the term 'Cryptonephridia' to understand its function and the organisms that possess it.
Determine which of the listed organisms is known to have Cryptonephridia based on biological literature.
Confirm that Mealworm beetle larvae are the correct choice as they are known to possess this type of excretory system.

text: Which of the following is true regarding the major difference between cellulose and glycogen [GLY-kuh-juhn]?
choices: Cellulose is a polymer of galactose [guh-LAK-thos], while glycogen is a polymer of glucose
Cellulose is mostly found in animal cells, while glycogen is mostly found in plant cells
Cellulose consists of beta glycosidic [gly-kuh-SY-dik] linkages, while glycogen consists of alpha glycosidic linkages
Cellulose is highly branched, while glycogen is linear
explainAnswer: Identify the structural components of cellulose and glycogen.
Understand that cellulose is made of beta glycosidic linkages, while glycogen is made of alpha glycosidic linkages.
Review the definitions of glycosidic linkages to differentiate between alpha and beta forms.
Eliminate the other choices based on the incorrect information about the structure and location of cellulose and glycogen.
Select the statement that accurately describes the glycosidic linkages in cellulose and glycogen.

text: Which of the following pairs of terms referring to the life cycle of land plants is mismatched with the correct ploidy?
explainAnswer: Identify the ploidy level of each term in the choices provided.
Recall that the integument is part of the ovule and is diploid, as it develops from the sporophyte generation.
Compare the identified ploidy levels with the terms given in the choices.
Determine which pair is mismatched based on the correct ploidy levels.

text: Identify all of the following four phyla [FYE-lah] that possess a segmented body plan: 1) Arthropoda ; 2) Mollusca [mull-US-kah]; 3) Nematoda; 4) Chordata [kor-DAH-tah].
explainAnswer: Recall the definition of a segmented body plan, which involves a body divided into repeating segments.
Identify the characteristics of each phylum listed: Arthropoda, Mollusca, Nematoda, and Chordata.
Determine which of these phyla exhibit segmentation: Arthropoda (insects, arachnids, etc.) and Chordata (vertebrates) are segmented.
Conclude that Mollusca and Nematoda do not have a segmented body plan.

text: What 1953 experiment, designed to test the Oparin-Haldane hypothesis, sought to emulate the conditions of early Earth in a laboratory?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms related to the Oparin-Haldane hypothesis, which discusses the origin of life.
Recall significant experiments in the field of abiogenesis that were conducted in the early 1950s.
Recognize that the experiment aimed to simulate early Earth conditions using a mixture of gases and energy sources.
Conclude that the experiment conducted by Stanley Miller and Harold Urey in 1953 is known as the Miller-Urey experiment.

text: What common second messenger is released after epinephrine binds to liver GPCRs and was the subject of the 1994 Nobel Prize?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of epinephrine in the body and its mechanism of action.
Research the signaling pathways activated by epinephrine binding to GPCRs in the liver.
Determine the second messengers involved in these pathways.
Recognize that cyclic AMP is a well-known second messenger and was highlighted in the 1994 Nobel Prize for its role in cellular signaling.

text: Which of the following is an example of simple squamous [SKWAY-mus] epithelium [eh-pih-THEEL-ee-um] ?
explainAnswer: Understand that simple squamous epithelium consists of a single layer of flat cells.
Identify the functions of different types of epithelium: simple squamous is involved in diffusion and filtration.
Evaluate each choice based on their structure: stomach lining and intestinal lining are not flat, while skin is stratified.
Recognize that lung lining (alveoli) is composed of simple squamous epithelium for efficient gas exchange.
Select lung lining as the correct answer.

text: What stage in animal development follows the blastula and is associated with the embryo folding inward?
explainAnswer: Identify the stages of animal development, starting from fertilization.
Recognize that the blastula is a hollow ball of cells formed after cleavage.
Understand that the next stage involves the process of gastrulation, where cells begin to fold inward.
Conclude that the stage following the blastula, characterized by this inward folding, is called the gastrula.

text: What leukocyte [LOO-koh-site] can have up to a five-lobed nucleus and plays a role in phagocytosis [fag-oh-sye-TOW-sis] of bacteria?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of cell being described as a leukocyte.
Recall the characteristics of leukocytes, particularly their nuclei structure.
Determine which leukocyte is known for having a multi-lobed nucleus.
Connect the function of phagocytosis to the identified leukocyte.
Conclude that the leukocyte with a five-lobed nucleus that performs phagocytosis of bacteria is a neutrophil.

text: Through what anatomical feature does water exit a sponge?
explainAnswer: Identify the anatomical features associated with sponges: osculum, ostium, atrium, and coelom.
Understand the function of each feature: ostia are small openings for water intake, while the osculum is the larger opening for water exit.
Recall that the osculum is the primary exit point for water in a sponge's filtration system.
Conclude that the correct answer is osculum, as it specifically refers to the exit of water.

text: Which of the following is not a characteristic of paedomorphic [ped-oh- MOOR-fik] amphibians?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of paedomorphic amphibians, which typically retain juvenile traits into adulthood.
Review the provided choices to determine which one does not align with the common traits of paedomorphic amphibians.
Recognize that delayed sexual maturity is a trait more associated with certain amphibians but not a defining characteristic of paedomorphosis.
Conclude that delayed sexual maturity is the correct answer as it does not fit the typical characteristics of paedomorphic amphibians.

text: If a protein’s environment is sufficiently altered, it can change shape or unfold entirely. What is the term for this process?
explainAnswer: Identify the process by which proteins change shape or unfold due to environmental changes.
Recall the specific term used in biochemistry for this phenomenon.
Confirm that the term is commonly known as denaturation.

text: Which of the following is NOT an adaptation for flight in birds?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics that are adaptations for flight in birds.
Evaluate each option to determine if it contributes to flight efficiency or capability.
Recognize that hollow bones, lack of a urinary bladder, and a keeled sternum all serve specific functions related to flight.
Conclude that solitary testis in males does not directly relate to flight adaptation.

text: To what phylum [FYE-lum] do most mushrooms belong?
explainAnswer: Recall that mushrooms are a type of fungi.
Identify the major phyla of fungi, which include Ascomycota and Basidiomycota.
Recognize that most mushrooms are classified under Basidiomycota.
Confirm that Basidiomycota is known for producing fruiting bodies, which are the mushrooms we see.

text: Identify all of the following three structures that are homologous [ha-MAWL-uh-gus] to a human hand: 1) Whale flipper; 2) Bat wing; 3) Bird claw.
explainAnswer: Understand that homologous structures are those that share a common ancestry, even if their functions differ.
Identify the skeletal structure of the human hand and compare it to the skeletal structures of the whale flipper, bat wing, and bird claw.
Determine that both the whale flipper and bat wing have similar bone arrangements to the human hand, indicating a common ancestor.
Conclude that the bird claw, while functional, does not share the same skeletal structure as the human hand and is therefore not homologous.

text: What type of selection is occurring if the fitness curve for a trait resembles a bimodal distribution?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the fitness curve for the trait in question.
Recognize that a bimodal distribution indicates two distinct peaks in fitness.
Understand that disruptive selection favors individuals at both extremes of the trait distribution.
Conclude that the presence of a bimodal distribution signifies disruptive selection is occurring.

text: The size of most mammalian cells is closest to which of the following?
explainAnswer: Consider the typical size range of mammalian cells, which is generally between 10 to 30 micrometers.
Convert the other units to micrometers for comparison: 1 picometer is 0.000001 micrometers, 1 millimeter is 1000 micrometers, and 1 centimeter is 10,000 micrometers.
Identify that 1 micrometer falls within the size range of mammalian cells, while the other options do not.

text: Identify all of the following three types of bacterial gene transfer that require cell-to-cell contact between the recipient and the donor: 1) Transformation; 2) Transduction; 3) Conjugation.
explainAnswer: Understand that transformation involves the uptake of free DNA from the environment, which does not require cell-to-cell contact.
Recognize that transduction is the transfer of DNA via a bacteriophage and also does not require direct contact between cells.
Identify that conjugation is the process where one bacterium transfers genetic material to another through direct contact, typically via a pilus.
Conclude that only conjugation requires cell-to-cell contact, making it the correct answer.

text: Identify all of the following four mutations that could result from a single- nucleotide substitution: 1) Silent; 2) Missense; 3) Nonsense; 4) Frameshift.
explainAnswer: Understand that a single-nucleotide substitution involves replacing one nucleotide with another in the DNA sequence.
Identify that a silent mutation does not change the amino acid sequence due to the redundancy of the genetic code.
Recognize that a missense mutation results in a different amino acid being incorporated into the protein due to the substitution.
Acknowledge that a nonsense mutation creates a premature stop codon, terminating protein synthesis early.
Note that a frameshift mutation is caused by insertions or deletions of nucleotides, not substitutions, so it is not included.

text: In what phylum [FYE-lum] is an octopus classified?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of an octopus, such as being a soft-bodied, marine animal with tentacles.
Recall that octopuses are known for their intelligence and complex behaviors.
Recognize that octopuses belong to a group of animals that are classified under the phylum Mollusca.
Confirm that Mollusca includes other creatures like snails, clams, and squids, which share similar traits.

text: MRSA is an infection by which of the following?
explainAnswer: Identify that MRSA stands for Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
Recognize that Staphylococcus aureus is a type of bacteria that is spherical in shape, also known as cocci.
Eliminate other options based on their shapes: rod-shaped (bacilli), rigid helical (spirilla), and non-rigid helical (spirochetes) do not describe MRSA.
Conclude that the correct answer is 'A spherical bacteria' based on the shape of Staphylococcus aureus.

text: In order for an animal to be classified as a coelomate [SEEL-oh-mate], it must have a body cavity that is completely lined with tissue from what germ layer?
explainAnswer: Understand the definition of a coelomate, which is an animal with a body cavity.
Identify the germ layers involved in animal development: ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm.
Recognize that the body cavity in coelomates is specifically lined with tissue derived from the mesoderm.
Conclude that the correct answer is mesoderm based on the definition and characteristics of coelomates.

text: Which of the following statements about monocots and dicots is NOT correct?
choices: Monocots have three holes in their pollen, while dicots only have one
Monocots have scattered vascular bundles, while dicot bundles are in a ring
Monocots lack a pith region in the stem, while dicots have a pith
Monocots have parallel venation in their leaves while dicots have netted veins
explainAnswer: Identify the key differences between monocots and dicots.
Review the characteristics of pollen structure in both groups.
Determine the correct number of pores in monocot and dicot pollen.
Compare the findings with the provided statements to identify the incorrect one.

text: Sickle cell anemia is an example of heterozygote [hetero-ZYE-goat] advantage because it protects against what disease?
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of heterozygote advantage, where individuals with one copy of a mutated gene have a survival benefit.
Identify that sickle cell anemia is caused by a mutation in the hemoglobin gene.
Research the relationship between sickle cell trait and resistance to malaria.
Conclude that individuals with the sickle cell trait are less likely to suffer severe effects from malaria, providing a survival advantage.

text: Identify all of the following three proteins that are transmembrane proteins: 1) Aquaporin; 2) Voltage- gated sodium channel; 3) Ras.
explainAnswer: Understand that transmembrane proteins span the entire membrane and have regions that are exposed to both the inside and outside of the cell.
Identify that aquaporin is a channel protein that facilitates water transport across cell membranes, thus it is a transmembrane protein.
Recognize that voltage-gated sodium channels are integral membrane proteins that allow sodium ions to pass through the membrane in response to voltage changes, making them transmembrane proteins.
Determine that Ras is a small GTPase that is primarily located on the inner surface of the plasma membrane and does not span the membrane, so it is not a transmembrane protein.

text: Identify all of the following three cell types that are leukocytes [LOO-koh-sites] : 1) Eosinophil [ee-oh-SIN-oh-fil] ; 2) Basophil [BAY-zoh-fil] ; 3) Erythrocyte [eh-RITH-roh-site] .
explainAnswer: Understand that leukocytes are white blood cells involved in the immune response.
Identify the function and classification of each cell type listed.
Recognize that eosinophils and basophils are both types of leukocytes.
Note that erythrocytes are red blood cells and not leukocytes.
Conclude that the correct answer includes eosinophils and basophils only.

text: What microsatellite genetic markers do forensic scientists typically use for crime scene DNA analysis?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of genetic markers used in forensic science.
Recall that microsatellites are short repetitive sequences in DNA.
Understand that Short Tandem Repeats (STRs) are a specific type of microsatellite.
Conclude that STRs are commonly used for crime scene DNA analysis.

text: Identify all of the following three structures that are homologous to the human arm: 1) Bat wing; 2) Cat hind leg; 3) Porpoise front flipper.
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of homology, which refers to structures that share a common ancestry.
Examine the skeletal structure of the human arm and compare it to the bat wing and porpoise front flipper, noting similarities in bone arrangement.
Determine that the bat wing and porpoise front flipper have similar bone structures to the human arm, indicating they are homologous.
Check the cat hind leg structure and note that it does not share the same bone arrangement as the human arm, thus it is not homologous.

text: A plant has a somatic chromosome number of 2n = 22. After a cell in this plant undergoes mitosis, how many chromosomes will the daughter cells each have?
explainAnswer: Identify the somatic chromosome number, which is given as 2n = 22.
Recognize that somatic cells are diploid, meaning they have two sets of chromosomes.
Understand that mitosis results in two daughter cells that are identical to the parent cell.
Conclude that each daughter cell will also have the same diploid number of chromosomes, which is 22.

text: Bacteria are able to become resistant to antibiotics by increasing their genetic variability through all of the following mechanisms EXCEPT:
explainAnswer: Identify the mechanisms listed: Conjugation, Transduction, Binary fission, and Transformation.
Understand that Conjugation, Transduction, and Transformation are methods of genetic exchange that increase variability.
Recognize that Binary fission is a method of asexual reproduction that does not increase genetic variability.
Conclude that Binary fission is the correct answer as it does not contribute to antibiotic resistance through increased genetic variability.

text: Which of the following processes does not change allele [Ah-LEEL] frequencies in a population?
explainAnswer: Understand that allele frequencies refer to how common an allele is in a population.
Recognize that genetic drift, natural selection, and gene flow all introduce changes to allele frequencies.
Identify that inbreeding increases the likelihood of certain alleles being expressed but does not change their overall frequency in the population.
Conclude that inbreeding is the process that does not change allele frequencies.

text: What human body cells contain H bands, Z disks and I bands?
explainAnswer: Recall the structure of skeletal muscle fibers, which include H bands, Z disks, and I bands.
Identify that H bands are regions of the sarcomere where only thick filaments (myosin) are present.
Recognize that Z disks are the boundaries of sarcomeres and I bands contain only thin filaments (actin).
Eliminate other cell types by noting that neurons, adipocytes, and osteocytes do not have these specific structures.

text: In female mammalian cells, the second X chromosome is generally silenced. What term is used to describe the condensed inactive X chromosome?
explainAnswer: Identify that the question refers to a specific biological phenomenon related to female mammals.
Recall that in female mammals, one of the two X chromosomes is typically inactivated.
Recognize that the inactivated X chromosome forms a condensed structure.
Know the specific term used to describe this condensed inactive X chromosome, which is 'Barr body'.

text: How many chambers are in a fish heart?
explainAnswer: Understand that fish have a two-chambered heart consisting of one atrium and one ventricle.
Recall that the atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body.
Recognize that the ventricle pumps the deoxygenated blood to the gills for oxygenation.
Conclude that the total number of chambers in a fish heart is 2.

text: You are drawing the Punnett square to tally the F2 generation of a trihybrid cross. How many entries are present within this square?
explainAnswer: Identify the number of traits involved in the trihybrid cross, which is 3 traits.
Determine the number of alleles for each trait, which is typically 2 (dominant and recessive).
Calculate the total number of combinations of alleles by raising the number of alleles (2) to the power of the number of traits (3), resulting in 2^3.
Evaluate 2^3, which equals 8, representing the number of different genotypes in the F2 generation.
Since each genotype can produce 8 combinations in a Punnett square, multiply 8 by itself (8 x 8) to find the total entries, resulting in 64.

text: Different species of hummingbirds have bills that vary in length and shape, matching the structure of the flowers on which they feed. Which of the following evolutionary scenarios best explains this diversity of hummingbird bill morphology?
choices: Coevolution of flowers and hummingbirds, leading to specialization of hummingbirds on particular flowers
Random mutation of plants to develop varying flower shapes, and subsequent evolution of hummingbird bills to match these shapes
Evolutionary race between flowers and hummingbirds, in which flowers become more extreme in shape to prevent nectar feeding
Evolution of various bill shapes, since all hummingbirds opportunistically feed on many different species of flower, regardless of shape
explainAnswer: Identify the relationship between hummingbirds and flowers based on their feeding habits.
Consider the concept of coevolution, where two species influence each other's evolution.
Evaluate the choices to see which one describes a mutual adaptation between hummingbirds and flowers.
Select the option that indicates specialization of hummingbirds to specific flower shapes, as this aligns with coevolution.

text: Identify all of the following three plants that associate parasitically with other plants: 1) Vanilla; 2) Mistletoe; 3) Venus flytrap.
explainAnswer: Understand the definition of parasitic plants, which derive some or all of their nutrients from other living plants.
Evaluate each plant: Vanilla is a hemiparasite but primarily grows as an epiphyte, not a true parasite.
Mistletoe is a true parasitic plant that attaches to host trees and derives nutrients from them.
The Venus flytrap is a carnivorous plant that captures insects for nutrients but does not parasitize other plants.
Conclude that the only plant that associates parasitically with others is Mistletoe.

text: What specific cell type in the stomach is responsible for production of pepsinogen?
explainAnswer: Recall the main functions of different cell types in the stomach.
Identify which cells are involved in enzyme production.
Determine which enzyme is specifically related to protein digestion.
Connect the enzyme pepsin to its inactive form, pepsinogen, and its source cell.

text: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding ticks and transmitted diseases?
choices: Female black legged ticks are only slightly better at transmitting Lyme disease than their male counterparts
The disease-causing agent in Lyme disease is the bacterium Borrelia burgdorferi [buh-REL- ee-uh boorg-dor-FE-ree]
The dog tick serves as a vector for Ricketssia ricketssia, the causative agent of Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever
The Lone Star Tick serves as a vector for disease-causing Rickettsia
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics of the ticks mentioned in each statement.
Research the transmission rates of Lyme disease between male and female black legged ticks.
Verify the roles of the dog tick and Lone Star Tick as vectors for their respective diseases.
Determine which statement contradicts established scientific knowledge about tick-borne diseases.

text: During what phase of meiosis [my-OH-sis] do sister chromatids separate?
answer: ANAPHASE II (DO NOT ACCEPT: ANAPHASE, ANAPHASE I)
explainAnswer: Understand that meiosis consists of two rounds: meiosis I and meiosis II.
Identify that sister chromatids are separated during the second round of meiosis, which is meiosis II.
Recognize that anaphase is the stage in both meiosis I and II where separation occurs, but sister chromatids specifically separate in anaphase II.
Conclude that the correct answer is anaphase II, as this is when sister chromatids are pulled apart.

text: One species resembles another species that is poisonous. What is this phenomenon called?
explainAnswer: Identify the key concept of one species resembling another for protection.
Recall the definitions of the terms provided in the choices.
Determine which term specifically describes a non-poisonous species mimicking a poisonous one.
Select the correct answer based on the definition of Batesian mimicry.

text: Identify all of the following three forms of reproductive barriers that are postzygotic [post-zye-GAW-tik] barriers: 1) Gametic [gah-MEE-tic] isolation; 2) Temporal isolation; 3) Hybrid breakdown.
explainAnswer: Understand the definition of postzygotic barriers, which occur after fertilization and affect hybrid offspring.
Review the three options provided: Gametic isolation, Temporal isolation, and Hybrid breakdown.
Identify that Gametic isolation prevents fertilization and Temporal isolation prevents mating, making them prezygotic barriers.
Recognize that Hybrid breakdown refers to reduced fitness in subsequent generations of hybrids, categorizing it as a postzygotic barrier.
Conclude that the only postzygotic barrier among the options is Hybrid breakdown.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true regarding a neuron at rest: 1) Voltage-gated sodium channels are mostly open; 2) Voltage-gated potassium channels are mostly open; 3) The sodium-potassium pump is hydrolyzing [HIGH-droh-lyzing] AT P.
explainAnswer: Understand that a neuron at rest has a resting membrane potential, typically around -70 mV.
Recognize that at rest, voltage-gated sodium channels are closed, not mostly open.
Note that voltage-gated potassium channels are also closed at rest, so they are not mostly open either.
Identify that the sodium-potassium pump is active at rest, continuously hydrolyzing ATP to maintain the concentration gradients of sodium and potassium.

text: Which of the following brain regions is primarily responsible for coordinating basic reflexes like swallowing and vomiting?
explainAnswer: Identify the brain regions listed in the choices.
Recall the functions associated with each brain region.
Determine which region is known for controlling basic reflexes.
Select the Medulla oblongata as it is responsible for reflexes like swallowing and vomiting.

text: Identify all of the following three structures that possess a double membrane: 1) Lysosome [LYE-soh-sohm] ; 2) Nucleus; 3) Ribosome [RYE-beh-sohme] .
explainAnswer: Understand that a double membrane structure has two lipid bilayers.
Identify that the nucleus is surrounded by a nuclear envelope, which consists of two membranes.
Recognize that lysosomes and ribosomes do not have double membranes; lysosomes have a single membrane and ribosomes are not membrane-bound organelles.
Conclude that the only structure with a double membrane from the options given is the nucleus.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of quantitative traits: 1) They are usually polygenic; 2) Without selection, they will be bimodally distributed in a population; 3) Eye color in fruit flies is a quantitative trait.
explainAnswer: Evaluate each statement regarding quantitative traits.
Identify that quantitative traits are typically influenced by multiple genes, making statement 1 true.
Recognize that quantitative traits usually have a continuous distribution rather than a bimodal distribution, making statement 2 false.
Determine that eye color in fruit flies is a discrete trait, not a quantitative trait, making statement 3 false.

text: Alpha cells of the pancreas secrete what hormone in response to low blood glucose?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of alpha cells in the pancreas.
Recall the function of hormones secreted by the pancreas.
Determine which hormone is released in response to low blood glucose levels.
