text: An XY baby with malfunctioning Sertoli cells cannot produce anti-Mullerian hormone. Which of the following phenotypes would result?
choices: Development of only a female reproductive tract.
Development of only a male reproductive tract.
Development of both a female and a male reproductive tract.
explainAnswer: Identify that Sertoli cells are responsible for producing anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH).
Understand that AMH inhibits the development of the female Mullerian ducts in males.
Recognize that without AMH, both male and female reproductive tracts can develop due to the presence of both Wolffian and Mullerian ducts.
Conclude that the phenotype resulting from malfunctioning Sertoli cells and lack of AMH would be the development of both reproductive tracts.

text: Order the following three blood vessels from first to last in terms of time needed to reach them from the right ventricle: 1) Pulmonary vein; 2) Pulmonary artery; 3) Hepatic portal vein.
explainAnswer: Identify the path of blood flow starting from the right ventricle.
Determine that blood first travels to the pulmonary artery to reach the lungs for oxygenation.
Next, recognize that oxygenated blood returns to the heart via the pulmonary vein.
Finally, understand that blood from the heart to the liver goes through the hepatic portal vein, which is the last in this sequence.

text: Which of the following glial cells is derived from hematopoietic stem cells?
explainAnswer: Understand that glial cells are non-neuronal cells in the nervous system.
Recognize that microglia are the immune cells of the central nervous system.
Identify that microglia originate from hematopoietic stem cells, unlike other glial cells.
Eliminate the other options (oligodendrocytes, ependymal cells, astrocytes) as they are derived from neural stem cells.

text: Brian is studying addiction to Genshin Impact, where gamers’ reward system overreleases dopamine. Which of the following regions of gamers’ brains should Brian inhibit to treat this addiction?
explainAnswer: Identify the brain regions involved in the reward system.
Understand that the ventral tegmental area (VTA) is crucial for dopamine release and reward processing.
Eliminate other options by knowing their primary functions are not directly related to addiction and dopamine release.
Conclude that inhibiting the VTA would reduce the overrelease of dopamine associated with addiction.

text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about fluorescence resonance electron energy transfer?
choices: It is extremely sensitive to small changes in distance
The energy is transferred through a nonradiative process
The radius of interaction is larger than the wavelength of light emitted
Measurements can be used to determine if two fluorophores are within a certain distance of each other
explainAnswer: Identify the key concepts related to fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET).
Evaluate each statement to determine its accuracy based on the principles of FRET.
Focus on the statement regarding the radius of interaction and compare it to the wavelength of light emitted.
Determine which statement contradicts established knowledge about FRET.
Conclude that the statement about the radius of interaction being larger than the wavelength of light emitted is NOT true.

text: In humans, negative feedback systems exist for many kinds of signals. In males, Sertoli cells prevent the overproduction of sperm by releasing what hormone which inhibits FSH release?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of Sertoli cells in the male reproductive system.
Understand that Sertoli cells are involved in the regulation of sperm production.
Recognize that these cells release a hormone to prevent overproduction of sperm.
Recall that the hormone released by Sertoli cells that inhibits FSH release is known as inhibin.
Conclude that the correct answer is inhibin.

text: Order the following three immune cells by increasing side scatter when conducting flow cytometry: 1) T cell; 2) Monocyte; 3) Basophil
explainAnswer: Understand that side scatter in flow cytometry correlates with the granularity and complexity of the cells.
Recognize that T cells are generally smaller and less granular than monocytes.
Identify that monocytes are larger and more granular than T cells but less than basophils.
Conclude that basophils, being the largest and most granular, will have the highest side scatter.

text: Order the following three types of muscle by increasing maximum V max (read:Vee-max) of their myosin ATPases: 1) Cardiac; 2) Skeletal; 3) Smooth.
explainAnswer: Understand that V max refers to the maximum rate of ATP hydrolysis by myosin ATPases in muscle types.
Recognize that smooth muscle has the lowest V max due to its slower contraction speed.
Identify that cardiac muscle has a moderate V max, allowing for faster contractions than smooth muscle but slower than skeletal muscle.
Conclude that skeletal muscle has the highest V max, enabling rapid contractions.
Order the muscle types from lowest to highest V max: Smooth (3), Cardiac (1), Skeletal (2).

text: Verno is studying a certain drug-protein complex localized to the membrane. He uses FRET (read:fret) to measure interaction between the drug and the protein. As his fluorescence signal increases in the FRET experiment, Verno photobleaches the membrane and finds that the fluorescence does not fully recover to its pre-bleach level. Which of the following is a logical conclusion he can make about the drug-protein complex?
choices: They are interacting and increasing membrane fluidity
They are interacting and decreasing membrane fluidity
They are not interacting and increasing membrane fluidity
They are not interacting and decreasing membrane fluidity
explainAnswer: Understand that FRET indicates interaction between the drug and protein when fluorescence increases.
Recognize that photobleaching typically allows for recovery of fluorescence if the molecules are mobile.
Note that the incomplete recovery of fluorescence suggests that the drug-protein complex is stabilizing the membrane.
Conclude that since the drug and protein are interacting and causing reduced mobility, they are decreasing membrane fluidity.

text: In order to translocate electrons from cytosolic NADH made during glycolysis to the electron transport chain, the import of malate into the mitochondrial matrix is coupled with the export of what intermediate formed from the transamination (read: trans-am-uh-NAY-shun) of oxaloacetate (read:ox-ah-low-ASS-uh-tayt)?
answer: ASPARTATE VISUAL BONUS 1) BIOLOGY –Short AnswerYour next bonus is visual. Shown in the image is the common garden phlox (read:flox). Answer the following two questions: 1) To what order of insects do the pollinators of this flower belong to? 2) This plant would be expected to produce pollen with how many pores? 1) LEPIDOPTERA; 2) 3
explainAnswer: Identify the process of transamination involving oxaloacetate.
Recognize that during transamination, oxaloacetate is converted to aspartate.
Understand that malate is imported into the mitochondrial matrix while aspartate is exported.
Conclude that aspartate is the intermediate formed from the transamination of oxaloacetate.

text: Identify all the following three hormones that are dervived from the same precursor as ACTH: 1) Vasopressin; 2) Melatonin; 3) Melanocyte-stimulating hormone.
answer: 3 ONLY VISUAL BONUS 8) BIOLOGY –Short AnswerYour next bonus is visual. The diagram depicts the relative proportion of a recessive deleterious allele in three populations colored red, blue, and green that are subjected to different conditions, leading to different mutation-selection equillibria. Identify all of the following three statements which are true: 1) All populations eventually reach fixation; 2) The blue population could be exposed to more intercalating agents than the population in red; 3) The green population could be in Hardy-Weinberg equillibrium. 2 AND 3
explainAnswer: Understand that ACTH is derived from pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC), which is a precursor for several hormones.
Identify which of the listed hormones are derived from POMC: Melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH) is one of them.
Determine that vasopressin and melatonin are not derived from POMC, thus only MSH is correct.
For the second part, analyze each statement based on population genetics principles.

Recognize that populations can reach fixation under certain conditions, and that the blue population may have higher mutation rates, while the green population can be in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium if conditions are met.

text: A Winogradsky (read:WIN-no-GRAHD-skee) column is an open tube with mud and water containing a diverse microbial ecosystem. Assuming they can are able to grow in such a column, order the following three microbes by where they would be found from top to bottom. 1) C. difficile; 2) Cyanobacteria; 3) Yeast.
answer: 2, 3, 1 VISUAL BONUS 18) BIOLOGY –Short AnswerYour next bonus is visual. Shown in the image is a Wright- Giemsa (read:rite-geem-sa) stain of a sample of blood cells collected from a patient with cancer. Answer the following two questions: 1) Identify the cells labeled A and B; 2) The cells known as B undergo what process to release cytotoxic compounds from secretory vesicles? 1) 1 IS EOSINOPHIL, 2 IS LYMPHOCYTE 2) DE- GRANULATION
explainAnswer: Identify the environmental conditions in a Winogradsky column, noting that light is present at the top and anaerobic conditions exist at the bottom.
Recognize that Cyanobacteria, which perform photosynthesis, would thrive at the top where light is available.
Determine that Yeast, which can grow in various conditions, would be found in the middle layer where some organic matter is present.
Conclude that C. difficile, an anaerobic bacterium, would be located at the bottom where oxygen is limited.

text: Jonathan takes a enzyme called X, reversibly inhibits it 3 ways, and then measures the Km of the enzyme after inhibition. Order the following three types of inhibition by increasing Km of X: 1) Noncompetitive; 2) Uncompetitive; 3) Competitive.
explainAnswer: Understand that Km represents the affinity of an enzyme for its substrate, with a lower Km indicating higher affinity.
Recognize that competitive inhibition increases Km because it requires a higher substrate concentration to reach half-maximal velocity.
Note that noncompetitive inhibition does not change Km because the enzyme can still bind substrate, but the overall rate is reduced.
Identify that uncompetitive inhibition decreases Km because it stabilizes the enzyme-substrate complex, effectively increasing affinity.
Order the types of inhibition based on their effects on Km: uncompetitive (decreases Km), noncompetitive (no change in Km), and competitive (increases Km).

text: In a particular ecosystem at equilibrium, milk snakes are Batesian (read:bates-ian) mimics of Sonoran coral snakes and Texas coral snakes are Mertensian (read:mer-tense-ian) mimics of Sonoran coral snakes. Order the following three species by increasing relative population change after a non-native predatory falcon species is introduced to this ecosystem: 1) Milk snake, 2) Sonoran coral snake, 3) Texas coral snake
explainAnswer: Identify the role of each snake species in the ecosystem: milk snakes are Batesian mimics, while Texas coral snakes are Mertensian mimics of Sonoran coral snakes.

Understand that Batesian mimics (milk snakes) benefit from the warning coloration of the toxic Sonoran coral snakes, while Mertensian mimics (Texas coral snakes) are also toxic but are less favored by predators.
Consider the impact of the introduction of a non-native predatory falcon, which will likely target the less defended species first.

Determine that the milk snake, being a non-toxic mimic, will suffer the most population decline, followed by the Texas coral snake, which has some toxicity but is still at risk, and finally the Sonoran coral snake, which is toxic and thus less likely to be preyed upon.
Order the species by their expected population change: milk snake (1), Texas coral snake (3), and Sonoran coral snake (2).

text: Cobalamin is required for the regeneration of which of the other vitamins?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of cobalamin (vitamin B12) in the body, particularly in relation to other vitamins.
Research the relationship between cobalamin and folic acid, noting that cobalamin is necessary for the conversion of homocysteine to methionine, which is linked to folate metabolism.
Eliminate the other options by confirming that they do not have a direct dependency on cobalamin for their function or regeneration.
Conclude that folic acid is the correct answer based on its established connection with cobalamin.

text: Identify all of the following three synaptic junctions in which acetylcholine is the primary neurotransmitter: 1) Parasympathetic (read:parr-uh-sim-puh-THETik) preganglionic (read:pree-gang-glee-ON-ik); 2) Parasympathetic postganglionic (read:postgang-glee-ON-ik); 3) Sympathetic preganglionic.
explainAnswer: Recall that acetylcholine is the primary neurotransmitter in both the parasympathetic and sympathetic nervous systems.
Identify that in the parasympathetic system, both preganglionic and postganglionic neurons release acetylcholine.
Recognize that sympathetic preganglionic neurons also release acetylcholine before synapsing with postganglionic neurons.
Conclude that all three synaptic junctions listed utilize acetylcholine as their primary neurotransmitter.

text: Identify all of the following three organisms that underwent a secondary endosymbiosis of a red algae: 1) The causative agent of african sleeping sickness; 2) The organism for which the Anopholes mosquito is the sole vector for; 3) The organisms that cause red tide.
explainAnswer: Identify the organisms listed in the question: the causative agent of African sleeping sickness (Trypanosoma brucei), the organism transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes (Plasmodium), and the organisms that cause red tide (dinoflagellates).
Research which of these organisms are known to have undergone secondary endosymbiosis of red algae.
Determine that Plasmodium (the malaria-causing organism) and certain dinoflagellates are the ones that have undergone this process.
Conclude that the correct answers are the organism for which the Anopheles mosquito is the sole vector (Plasmodium) and the organisms that cause red tide (dinoflagellates).

text: When the ciliary body overproduces vitreous humor, it can lead to what condition in the eye that causes increased intraocular pressure, and can be tested for with a blow test?
answer: GLAUCOMA VISUAL BONUS 13) BIOLOGY –Short AnswerYour next bonus is visual. Shown in the image are three organisms. A is a type of lungfish, and C is a type of salamander. Answer the following two questions: 1) By number, identify all of the following three traits that are shared among these organisms: 1) Amniotic egg; 2) Mineralized skeleton; 3) Jaws; 2) Identify which of these organisms would contain a spiral valve. 1) 3 ONLY; 2) B
explainAnswer: Identify the role of the ciliary body in the eye and its relationship to vitreous humor production.
Understand that excessive production of vitreous humor can lead to increased intraocular pressure.
Recognize that this condition is known as glaucoma.
Recall that glaucoma can be tested for using a blow test.

text: Smoltification (read:smolt-ification) in salmon, which is the physiological adaptation to living in salty water, is induced by the release of what hormone, which is also produced by the zona fasciculata (read:zona-fas-ick-you-laat-ah) in humans?
explainAnswer: Identify the process of smoltification and its significance in salmon.
Research the hormones involved in smoltification and their sources.
Determine which hormone is produced by the zona fasciculata in humans.
Connect the hormone identified with its role in both salmon and humans.
Conclude that the hormone responsible for smoltification is cortisol.

text: You are investigating different structures cells form during cytokinesis. You have stained cells undergoing cytokinesis with DAPI (read:dap-ee) and an antibody against tubulin. Which of the following groups of organisms would be distinguishable from charophytes? 1) Chlorophytes; 2) Land plants; 3) Red algae.
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics of charophytes and how they differ from chlorophytes, land plants, and red algae.
Understand that charophytes are closely related to land plants and share certain features with them.
Recognize that chlorophytes and red algae have distinct traits that set them apart from charophytes.
Determine that both chlorophytes and red algae can be distinguished from charophytes based on their cellular structures and reproductive strategies.

text: Quinolones (read:quinn-o-lones) and camptothecins (read: camp-toh-theh-kins) are antibiotics that inhibit a certain enzyme to cause bacterial chromosomes to become toroidally shaped or plectonemic (read:pleck-toe-neem-ic) after replication. What general class of enzymes in DNA synthesis do they inhibit?
answer: TOPOISOMERASES VISUAL BONUS 4) BIOLOGY –Short AnswerYour next bonus is visual. You are studying the DNA replication fork in a cell using FRET (read:fret). A donor fluorophore is attached to DNA helicase, and acceptor fluorophores are attached on DNA polymerases. Answer the following two questions: 1) Which of the following diagrams represents the signal on the leading strand? 2) Which of the following diagrams represents the signal on the lagging strand? 1) E; 2) B
explainAnswer: Identify the role of quinolones and camptothecins in bacterial DNA replication.
Recognize that these antibiotics target enzymes involved in managing DNA topology.
Determine that the general class of enzymes affected by these antibiotics is topoisomerases.
For the visual bonus, understand the function of DNA helicase and DNA polymerases in the replication fork.
Analyze the diagrams to identify which represents the leading strand and which represents the lagging strand based on the direction of replication.

text: Order the following three disorders of the eye in terms of increasing distance of the region affected to the retina: 1) Cataract; 2) Macular degeneration; 3) Conjunctivitus.
answer: 2, 1, 3 VISUAL BONUS 9) BIOLOGY –Short AnswerYour next bonus is visual. Shown in the image is an image of the heart of a patient suffering from low blood oxygenation. Answer the following three questions: 1) This image is produced with what technique, which uses ultrasound? 2) Identify the structure labeled by the red arrow, which is a temporary hole between the two atria present at birth; 3) The failure of the previous hole to close causes which of the labeled chambers, A or B, to have less oxygenated blood than usual? 1) ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY; 2) FORAMEN OVALE 3) B.
explainAnswer: Identify the regions affected by each disorder: cataract affects the lens, macular degeneration affects the macula, and conjunctivitis affects the conjunctiva.
Determine the distance of each region from the retina: the lens is closer than the macula, and the conjunctiva is the farthest from the retina.
Order the disorders based on their distance from the retina, starting with macular degeneration, followed by cataract, and finally conjunctivitis.

text: Fluoroacetic acid (read:floor-o-uh-cetic) is highly toxic because it interferes with a particular enzyme in the Krebs cycle, resulting in the buildup of citrate. What enzyme does fluoroacetic acid inhibit?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of fluoroacetic acid in the Krebs cycle.
Research the enzymes involved in the Krebs cycle and their functions.
Determine which enzyme is responsible for the conversion of citrate to isocitrate.
Conclude that the enzyme inhibited by fluoroacetic acid is aconitase.

text: Alice’s fruit fly embryo sample and Bob’s basidiomycete (read: buh-SID-ee-oh-MY-seat) sample both contain cells that possess multiple nuclei. Identify all of the following three statements that are true about their samples: 1) The formation of both samples could be recreated by applying a microtubule depolymerization inhibitor to a cell; 2) Bob’s samples are collectible through the majority of the basidiomycete lifetime; 3) If Alice and Bob each sequence the DNA within the nuclei of their own samples, Alice would observe less SNPs within her sample compared to Bob.
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the samples: Alice's fruit fly embryos and Bob's basidiomycete, noting that both have multiple nuclei.
Evaluate statement 1 regarding microtubule depolymerization inhibitors and their effects on cell division, determining if it applies to both samples.
Assess statement 2 about the collectibility of Bob's basidiomycete samples throughout its life cycle, confirming its validity.
Analyze statement 3 by comparing the expected SNPs in the DNA of Alice's and Bob's samples, considering the genetic diversity of the organisms.
Conclude which statements are true based on the evaluations of each statement.

text: Dr. Damon is prescribing MAO (read:maow) inhibitors. Which of the following diseases is he likely treating?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of MAO inhibitors, which are primarily used to increase levels of neurotransmitters in the brain.
Recall that Parkinson's disease is associated with low levels of dopamine, a neurotransmitter.
Consider the other options: ALS and Addison's disease do not primarily involve neurotransmitter levels, and ADHD is typically treated with stimulants rather than MAO inhibitors.
Conclude that MAO inhibitors are most commonly used in the treatment of Parkinson's disease.

text: The presence of antinuclear antibodies in serum most likely indicates which of the following diseases?
explainAnswer: Understand that antinuclear antibodies (ANAs) are often associated with autoimmune diseases.
Recall that systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a well-known autoimmune disease that frequently tests positive for ANAs.
Evaluate the other options: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia, Cushing syndrome, and hemolytic anemia do not typically present with ANAs.
Conclude that the presence of antinuclear antibodies most likely indicates systemic lupus erythematosus.

text: The dense bodies of smooth muscle are analagous to which of the following structures in skeletal muscle?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of dense bodies in smooth muscle, which anchor actin filaments and facilitate contraction.
Recall that Z discs in skeletal muscle serve a similar purpose by anchoring thin filaments and defining the boundaries of sarcomeres.
Compare the roles of dense bodies and Z discs in muscle contraction to establish their analogy.
Select the correct answer based on the structural and functional similarities between dense bodies and Z discs.

text: Identify all of the following three types of cellular junctions that use connexins: 1) Gap junction; 2) Adherens junction; 3) Desmosomes.
explainAnswer: Understand that connexins are proteins that form channels between adjacent cells.
Recognize that gap junctions are specialized connections that allow for direct communication between cells through these channels.
Identify that adherens junctions and desmosomes are types of junctions that provide structural support and do not use connexins.

text: During an enzyme assay, initial product formation is rapid before leveling off into a slower, steady-state rate. This burst-phase kinetic behavior is typically observed when the enzyme forms a covalent intermediate during catalysis. Which of the following enzymes most likely exhibits this behavior?
explainAnswer: Identify the enzymes listed and their general mechanisms of action.
Recognize that chymotrypsin is a serine protease that forms a covalent intermediate during its catalytic cycle.
Consider the burst-phase kinetic behavior associated with enzymes that form covalent intermediates.
Eliminate other options that do not typically exhibit this behavior based on their mechanisms.
Conclude that chymotrypsin is the enzyme that most likely exhibits burst-phase kinetics.

text: In order for Theca cells to convert testosterone to estrogen, they must produce what enzyme that converts androgens to estrogens?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of Theca cells in hormone production.
Understand the process of converting androgens to estrogens.
Recall the specific enzyme responsible for this conversion.
Conclude that the enzyme needed is aromatase.

text: GIP (read:G-I-P) and GLP are both glucagon peptides that induce the release of insulin upon oral intake of food. They both belong to what more specific group of hormones, which are responsible for decreasing blood sugar?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of GIP and GLP in relation to insulin and blood sugar.
Recognize that both GIP and GLP are involved in the regulation of blood sugar levels.
Determine the broader category of hormones that includes GIP and GLP based on their function.
Conclude that the specific group of hormones responsible for decreasing blood sugar is called incretins.

text: Alex is using tandem mass spectrometry in his laboratory. Which of the following goals is he trying to accomplish?
explainAnswer: Understand that tandem mass spectrometry is a technique used for analyzing the composition of molecules.
Recognize that it is commonly used for identifying and sequencing proteins due to its ability to analyze complex mixtures.
Eliminate options that are less relevant to mass spectrometry, such as DNA sequencing and RNA sequencing.
Conclude that the most appropriate goal for tandem mass spectrometry in this context is protein sequencing.

text: Katya performs an experiment in which she isolates human mitochondria and places them into a solution of Tris-HCl buffered at pH 9.5. Given that the outer mitochondrial membrane is permable to protons, what will happen to the rate of ATP production, and the oxygen consumption of the cell, respectively?
explainAnswer: Identify that the outer mitochondrial membrane is permeable to protons, which means protons can freely move in and out.
Recognize that a high pH (9.5) indicates a lower concentration of protons (H+) in the solution compared to the inside of the mitochondria.
Understand that this proton gradient is essential for ATP production via oxidative phosphorylation; a decrease in the gradient will reduce ATP synthesis.
Note that oxygen consumption is linked to the electron transport chain, which will continue to function despite the reduced ATP production, leading to increased oxygen consumption.

text: Often considered the most abundant protein in the world, which protein is responsible for fixing carbon into RuBP (read:roo-bee-pee) in the Calvin cycle?
explainAnswer: Recall the key processes of photosynthesis, particularly the Calvin cycle.
Identify the main functions and components involved in the Calvin cycle.
Recognize that RuBP (ribulose bisphosphate) is a substrate in the Calvin cycle.
Determine which enzyme is responsible for the fixation of carbon into RuBP.
Conclude that the most abundant protein involved in this process is RUBISCO.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of mitochondria: 1) They contain circular chromosomes; 2) They have a higher pH in the matrix than the intermembrane space; 3) The folds that increase surface area in them are called cisternae.
explainAnswer: Evaluate the structure of mitochondria and confirm that they contain circular chromosomes, similar to prokaryotic cells.
Analyze the pH levels in mitochondria, noting that the matrix has a higher pH than the intermembrane space due to proton concentration differences.
Recognize that the folds in mitochondria are called cristae, not cisternae, which are associated with the endoplasmic reticulum.
Conclude that statements 1 and 2 are true, while statement 3 is false.

text: Which of the following substances would diffuse the fastest through a mammalian cell lipid bilayer?
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of the substances listed, focusing on size and polarity.
Recall that nonpolar molecules generally diffuse faster through lipid bilayers than polar molecules.
Determine the polarity of each substance: water and glucose are polar, while carbon dioxide is nonpolar.
Consider the size of the molecules; carbon dioxide is relatively small compared to glucose.
Conclude that carbon dioxide will diffuse the fastest due to its nonpolarity and smaller size.

text: Alice and Bob have a daughter named Christine. If Alice has a disease while Bob does not, which of the following inheritance patterns would lead to Christine having the lowest probability of having the disease?
explainAnswer: Identify the inheritance patterns and their implications for offspring based on the parents' genotypes.
Recognize that Alice has the disease, indicating she carries the disease allele, while Bob does not.
Determine that in X-linked recessive inheritance, daughters inherit one X chromosome from each parent, and since Bob does not have the disease, he can only pass on a normal X chromosome.

Conclude that Christine would only inherit the disease allele from Alice if it were X-linked recessive, resulting in the lowest probability of her having the disease compared to the other inheritance patterns.

text: Todd is studying a certain plant ground tissue under the microscope that stains red with phloroglucinol-HCl (read:florr-oh-GLOO-suh-nol). He notices that the tissue is extremely lignified, has secondary cell walls, and is also dead at maturity. Which of the following classes of tissue is he likely studying?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the tissue: extremely lignified, has secondary cell walls, and is dead at maturity.
Recall that sclerenchyma is known for having thick secondary cell walls and being dead at maturity.
Eliminate other options: aerenchyma is involved in gas exchange, parenchyma is living and not lignified, and collenchyma has unevenly thickened cell walls and is also living.
Conclude that the tissue Todd is studying, based on its characteristics, is sclerenchyma.

text: Starting from the thylakoid space of a chloroplast, the Magic School Bus would like to travel to the inside of the nucleus of the same cell. How many membranes does the Magic School Bus need to travel through?
explainAnswer: Identify that the thylakoid space is located within the thylakoid membrane of the chloroplast.
Recognize that the chloroplast has an outer membrane and an inner membrane, totaling two membranes to exit the chloroplast.
Understand that the chloroplast is located within the cytoplasm, which is surrounded by the plasma membrane of the cell, adding one more membrane.
Acknowledge that the nucleus is surrounded by a double membrane, which consists of an inner and an outer nuclear membrane, adding two more membranes.
Sum the total membranes: 2 (chloroplast) + 1 (plasma) + 2 (nucleus) = 5 membranes.

text: Even when a person is upside down, it is possible to completely swallow a bolus through the action of which muscular mechanism?
explainAnswer: Identify the process involved in moving food through the digestive tract.
Understand that peristalsis is a series of wave-like muscle contractions.
Recognize that peristalsis can occur regardless of body position, including upside down.
Conclude that peristalsis is the muscular mechanism that allows swallowing in any position.

text: Which of the following is NOT a shared feature among archaea and bacteria?
explainAnswer: Identify the features listed in the question and understand what they mean.
Recall that both archaea and bacteria are prokaryotic, meaning they lack a nucleus and membrane-enclosed organelles.
Recognize that while bacteria typically do not have histones, archaea do have histones associated with their DNA.
Determine which feature is not shared by both groups, which leads to the conclusion that the lack of histones is the correct answer.

text: Found in cardiac muscle and made of desmosomes and gap junctions, what structures between cardiomyocytes occur at the Z line of the sarcomere?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of muscle tissue being referred to, which is cardiac muscle.
Recall the structural components associated with cardiac muscle cells, particularly desmosomes and gap junctions.
Understand the location of these structures, specifically at the Z line of the sarcomere.
Conclude that the structures formed by these components are known as intercalated discs.

text: Order the following three populations of rabbits in increasing effective population size: 1) 3 males, 3 females; 2) 1 male, 5 females; 3) 12 males, 2 females.
explainAnswer: Calculate the effective population size (Ne) for each population using the formula Ne = 4 * (number of males * number of females) / (number of males + number of females).
For population 1 (3 males, 3 females), Ne = 4 * (3 * 3) / (3 + 3) = 6.
For population 2 (1 male, 5 females), Ne = 4 * (1 * 5) / (1 + 5) = 3.33.
For population 3 (12 males, 2 females), Ne = 4 * (12 * 2) / (12 + 2) = 9.6.
Order the populations based on their Ne values: population 2 has the smallest Ne, followed by population 1, and then population 3.

text: The high temperatures in the denaturation step of PCR are intended to disrupt which type of bond that holds DNA strands together?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of bonds that hold the DNA strands together.
Recall that DNA is composed of two strands held together by base pairing.
Determine which bond type is responsible for the base pairing between the strands.
Recognize that hydrogen bonds are the weak interactions that hold the two strands of DNA together.
Conclude that the high temperatures in PCR disrupt hydrogen bonds.

text: Which of the following mutations in mRNA is silent?
explainAnswer: Identify the original codon and the mutated codon for each choice.
Translate each codon into its corresponding amino acid using the genetic code.
Determine if the mutated codon results in the same amino acid as the original codon.
Select the mutation that does not change the amino acid, indicating it is a silent mutation.

text: Which of the following traits is not characteristic of species adapted for living near carrying capacity?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of species adapted for living near carrying capacity, such as high parental care and few offspring.
Understand that semelparous species reproduce only once in their lifetime, which is not typical for stable populations near carrying capacity.
Recognize that a Type I survivorship curve indicates high survival rates for offspring, aligning with traits of species near carrying capacity.
Conclude that semelparity does not fit the pattern of traits associated with species living near carrying capacity.

text: Identify all of the following three lab techniques that require NTPs: 1) Sanger sequencing; 2) PCR; 3) Western blot.
explainAnswer: Understand that NTPs (nucleoside triphosphates) are essential for DNA synthesis.
Recognize that Sanger sequencing involves the incorporation of nucleotides during DNA replication.
Identify that PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) also requires NTPs for amplifying DNA.
Note that Western blotting is a protein analysis technique and does not involve nucleotides.

text: Retroviruses such as HIV use reverse transcriptase in their replication process. The genome of HIV is primarily made up of which of the following?
explainAnswer: Understand that retroviruses are a class of viruses that replicate in a host cell by reverse transcription.
Recall that reverse transcriptase is an enzyme that converts RNA into DNA.
Identify that HIV is a well-known retrovirus.
Recognize that the genome of HIV is primarily composed of RNA, specifically single stranded RNA.

text: Green smooth pea plants are dominant to yellow wrinkled pea plants. These two traits are completely linked. John crosses two true breeding smooth green and wrinkled yellow plants and self crosses the F1 generation. If a yellow offspring is picked among the F2 generation, what is the probability it is also smooth?
explainAnswer: Identify the genotypes of the true breeding smooth green and wrinkled yellow plants, which are GG (green) and ww (yellow) respectively.
Determine the genotype of the F1 generation, which will be all Gg (smooth green) since green is dominant.
Self-cross the F1 generation (Gg x Gg) to find the F2 generation genotypes, resulting in GG, Gg, and gg.
Recognize that the only possible genotypes for yellow offspring are gg, which means they cannot be smooth.
Conclude that the probability of a yellow offspring being smooth is 0.

text: Whereas a closed circulatory system pumps blood through closed vessels, an open circulatory system instead pumps what fluid through the hemocoel (read: HEE-moh-seel)?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question, such as 'closed circulatory system', 'open circulatory system', and 'hemocoel'.
Understand that in an open circulatory system, the fluid that circulates is not blood but a different type of fluid.
Recall that the fluid in an open circulatory system is known as hemolymph.
Conclude that the correct answer is hemolymph based on the definitions of the circulatory systems.

text: In the tracheal systems of insects, the trachea are kept open to the environment by rings made of what molecule?
explainAnswer: Identify the structure of the tracheal system in insects and its function.
Recall the materials that provide structural support in biological systems.
Consider the common molecules associated with exoskeletons and respiratory systems in arthropods.
Recognize that chitin is a key component that provides rigidity and support in these structures.
Conclude that the rings keeping the trachea open are made of chitin.

text: Spongocytes and choanocytes (read:koh-ANN-oh-sites) are cell types found in which of the following phyla of organisms?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms: spongocytes and choanocytes.
Recall that spongocytes are specialized cells associated with sponges.
Recognize that choanocytes are also characteristic of sponges and help in water flow and feeding.
Determine which phylum includes sponges, which is Porifera.
Select Porifera as the correct answer based on the association of these cell types.

text: Neurons 1 and 2 are both synapsed on neuron 3. When neuron 1 is activated, neuron 3 undergoes an action potential. When neuron 1 and 2 are both activated, neuron 3 doesn’t undergo an action potential. Which of the following could be true of neuron 2’s effects on neuron 3?
choices: The synapse between them is experiencing long term depression
The synapse between them is experiencing long term potentiation
It increases the permeability of neuron 3 for sodium ions
It increases the permeability of neuron 3 for chloride ions
explainAnswer: Identify the role of neuron 1 and neuron 2 in relation to neuron 3.
Recognize that neuron 1 can activate neuron 3, while the combined activation of neuron 1 and 2 does not lead to an action potential in neuron 3.
Consider the possible effects of neuron 2 on neuron 3, focusing on inhibitory versus excitatory influences.
Determine that if neuron 2 inhibits neuron 3, it could increase the permeability for chloride ions, which would hyperpolarize neuron 3.
Conclude that the correct answer is that neuron 2 increases the permeability of neuron 3 for chloride ions.

text: Caleb is studying certain amino acid residues in the insulin receptor that are phosphorylated upon dimerization (read:dye-murr-ih-ZAY-shun) of the receptor. Which amino acid, which is chemically similar to phenylalanine, is he studying?
explainAnswer: Identify the amino acids listed in the choices: Threonine, Tyrosine, Alanine, Histidine.
Determine which of these amino acids is chemically similar to phenylalanine, which is an aromatic amino acid.
Recognize that tyrosine contains a hydroxyl group attached to the aromatic ring, making it chemically similar to phenylalanine.
Eliminate the other options as they do not share the aromatic structure with phenylalanine.
Conclude that the correct answer is Tyrosine.

text: Jonah is trying to measure the transcriptome of T-cells that he treated with a promising phase 1 trial antitumor drug. Which of the following techniques could he NOT use to measure the transcriptome?
explainAnswer: Identify the techniques listed and their primary functions in measuring RNA or transcriptome.
Determine which techniques are specifically designed for analyzing RNA levels or sequences.
Recognize that Fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) is primarily used for studying protein interactions, not RNA measurement.
Conclude that FRET cannot be used to measure the transcriptome, while the other techniques can.

text: Order the following three sites by when a charged tRNA would encounter them on the ribosome from earliest to latest: 1) A site; 2) E site; 3) P site.
explainAnswer: Identify the function of each site on the ribosome: A site (aminoacyl), P site (peptidyl), and E site (exit).
Recognize that charged tRNA first enters the ribosome at the A site where it binds to the mRNA codon.
Understand that after the tRNA in the A site transfers its amino acid to the growing polypeptide chain in the P site, it moves to the P site.
Finally, after the tRNA has released its amino acid, it exits the ribosome through the E site.

text: Caleb is studying the epigenome of his retina cells and notices that the region around the myoglobin protein is heavily compacted. Identify all of the following three treatments that could decrease the compaction in this region: 1) Removing methylated cytosines; 2) Adding acetyl groups to the histone tails; 3) Removing phosphate groups from the histone tails.
explainAnswer: Understand that DNA compaction is influenced by methylation and acetylation of histones.
Recognize that removing methylated cytosines can lead to a more open chromatin structure.
Identify that adding acetyl groups to histone tails reduces positive charges, leading to decreased interaction with negatively charged DNA.
Note that removing phosphate groups from histone tails does not significantly affect compaction.
Conclude that treatments 1 and 2 would decrease compaction in the region around the myoglobin protein.

text: The first time Caleb pets a turtle, it retracts back into its shell. However, after petting the turtle many more times, it no longer retracts into its shell. What type of learning is this an example of?
explainAnswer: Identify the behavior of the turtle when first petted, which is to retract into its shell.
Recognize that repeated exposure to the same stimulus (petting) leads to a decrease in the turtle's response.
Understand that this decrease in response to a repeated stimulus is a key characteristic of habituation.
Conclude that the turtle's change in behavior after multiple pettings is an example of habituation.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true about mycorrhizae (read:my-koh-RYE-zee): 1) Most mycorrhizal fungi are glomeromycetes (read:glomer-oh-MY-seets); 2) Mycorrhizae primarily help absorb nitrogenous nutrients; 3) Nutrients taken up by ectomycorrhizae must enter the apoplast before they can enter the symplast.
explainAnswer: Identify the type of fungi associated with mycorrhizae and confirm that most are indeed glomeromycetes.
Evaluate the role of mycorrhizae in nutrient absorption, noting that they primarily assist in phosphorus uptake rather than nitrogen.
Understand the distinction between ectomycorrhizae and endomycorrhizae, focusing on how nutrients enter the plant cells through the apoplast in ectomycorrhizae.

text: Which of the following chambers of the heart has the thickest myocardium?
explainAnswer: Understand that the myocardium is the muscular layer of the heart responsible for contraction.
Recall that the left ventricle pumps blood to the entire body, requiring more force than the other chambers.
Compare the functions of each chamber to determine which requires the thickest muscle layer.
Conclude that the left ventricle has the thickest myocardium due to its role in systemic circulation.

text: James has just been prescribed Zestril to lower his blood pressure. Drugs like Zestril work because they inhibit the enzyme ACE (read:ace), which normally catalyzes the production of what vasoconstrictive hormone?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of ACE in the body.
Recall that ACE is involved in the renin-angiotensin system.
Understand that ACE catalyzes the conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II.
Recognize that angiotensin II is a vasoconstrictive hormone.
Conclude that the correct answer is angiotensin II.

text: Which of the following states would lead to the highest expression of lac operon?
explainAnswer: Identify the conditions that activate the lac operon, which are high levels of lactose and low levels of glucose.
Understand that high lactose levels lead to the production of allolactose, which binds to the repressor and allows transcription.
Recognize that low glucose levels increase cAMP, which activates CAP, enhancing the transcription of the lac operon.
Evaluate each choice based on these conditions to determine which combination maximizes lac operon expression.

text: The statoliths (read:stay-toe-liths) that help plant roots sense gravity are specialized versions of what starch-storing plant organelle?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of statoliths in plants and their role in gravity sensing.
Recall that statoliths are specialized structures derived from a type of organelle.
Determine which organelle is responsible for starch storage in plants.
Conclude that the correct answer is the specialized version of the starch-storing organelle, which is amyloplast.

text: Plant cells do not lyse in a hypotonic environment due to the prescence of what cellulose-containing structure?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question, such as 'plant cells', 'hypotonic environment', and 'cellulose-containing structure'.
Recall the function of plant cell structures and their roles in maintaining cell integrity.
Consider how a hypotonic environment affects cells and what structures prevent lysis.
Conclude that the structure that provides support and prevents lysis in plant cells is the cell wall.

text: Which of the following DNA strands, if annealed with their complementary strand, would have the lowest melting point?
explainAnswer: Identify the GC content of each DNA strand, as GC pairs form three hydrogen bonds compared to two for AT pairs.
Calculate the percentage of GC pairs in each strand: TTAGAAT has 0%, ACTCAGA has 33%, ACTACGT has 50%, and GCGCCTT has 75%.
Determine that the strand with the lowest GC content will have the lowest melting point due to fewer hydrogen bonds.
Conclude that TTAGAAT, with 0% GC content, has the lowest melting point.

text: Elk often live in groups, and the male is highly ornamented while the females are not highly ornameted. Knowing this, what kind of mating system do elk likely follow?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the mating system options provided.
Recognize that in polygyny, one male mates with multiple females, which aligns with the description of highly ornamented males attracting females.
Consider the social structure of elk, where males compete for access to females, supporting the polygynous system.
Eliminate other options like monogamy and polyandry, as they do not fit the observed behavior of elk.

text: Which of the following processes is least likely to be disrupted by the introduction of a calcium chelator?
choices: Formation of a fertilization envelope in a zygote
Action potential initiation in a sensory neuron
Long term potentiation in the brain
explainAnswer: Identify the role of calcium in each process listed in the choices.
Determine which process relies least on calcium for its initiation or function.
Evaluate how calcium chelators affect calcium-dependent processes.
Conclude that action potential initiation in a sensory neuron is primarily dependent on sodium and not directly on calcium.

text: Golden Gate and Gibson assembly both use what class of bacterial enzymes to cleave DNA fragments for plasmid assembly?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which involves DNA manipulation techniques.
Recall the types of enzymes commonly used in molecular biology for cutting DNA.
Recognize that both Golden Gate and Gibson assembly utilize specific enzymes for DNA cleavage.
Conclude that the class of enzymes used for this purpose is known as restriction enzymes.

text: Identify all of the following three vitamins that would be excreted in urine in significant amounts: 1) Thiamine; 2) Niacin; 3) Ascorbic acid.
explainAnswer: Understand that water-soluble vitamins are typically excreted in urine when consumed in excess.
Identify that thiamine (Vitamin B1), niacin (Vitamin B3), and ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) are all water-soluble vitamins.
Recognize that since these vitamins are not stored in the body, any excess intake will be eliminated through urine.
Conclude that all three vitamins listed will be excreted in significant amounts in urine.

text: A woman passes on the slay trait to all six of her children, yet her brother does not pass on the trait to any of his 54 offspring. What inheritance pattern is most likely?
explainAnswer: Identify that mitochondrial traits are passed from mother to all offspring regardless of sex.
Note that the woman passes the slay trait to all six of her children, indicating maternal inheritance.
Recognize that the brother does not pass the trait to any of his children, which aligns with mitochondrial inheritance as it is not passed through males.
Eliminate other inheritance patterns such as X linked recessive and Y linked, as they do not fit the described scenario.

text: Emilia is studying a certain eukaryote. During mitosis the spindles pass through the nuclear envelope through cytoplasmic channels, and the nucleus does not dissolve. Which of the following organisms could this be?
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics of the organisms listed in the choices.
Recall that dinoflagellates have a unique form of mitosis where the nuclear envelope remains intact.
Eliminate the other options based on their typical mitotic processes.
Confirm that dinoflagellates are known for their spindles passing through the nuclear envelope via cytoplasmic channels.

text: In the beta oxidation of fatty acids, a certain two carbon intermediate is released upon each oxidation cycle. What is the identity of this two carbon intermediate?
explainAnswer: Recall the process of beta oxidation, which involves the breakdown of fatty acids.
Identify that each cycle of beta oxidation removes a two-carbon unit from the fatty acid chain.
Recognize that the two-carbon unit released is in the form of acetyl-CoA.
Confirm that acetyl-CoA is the product of the complete oxidation of fatty acids.

text: Identify all of the following three agents that are involved in the positive feedback cycle during labor: 1) Prostaglandins; 2) Oxytocin; 3) PYY.
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of positive feedback in the context of labor.
Identify the roles of prostaglandins and oxytocin in stimulating uterine contractions.
Recognize that PYY is not involved in the labor process.
Conclude that the correct agents involved in the positive feedback cycle during labor are prostaglandins and oxytocin.

text: While in mammals, females have separate external openings for the reproductive, digestive, and excretory systems, nonmammalian vertebrates often have a common opening for these three tracts. What is the name of this structure, where eggs exit chickens?
explainAnswer: Identify the common anatomical structure in nonmammalian vertebrates that serves multiple functions.
Recall that this structure is involved in the excretion and reproduction processes.
Consider the specific example of birds, such as chickens, to relate it to the question.
Conclude that the term for this common opening is 'cloaca'.

text: In the breakdown of erythrocytes, the iron-porphyrin complex is broken down into Fe<sup>2+</sup> and what pigmented compound that is a component of bile?
explainAnswer: Identify the components involved in the breakdown of erythrocytes.
Recognize that hemoglobin is broken down into heme and globin.
Understand that the heme group is further broken down into iron and a pigmented compound.
Recall that the pigmented compound produced from heme breakdown is bilirubin.
Conclude that bilirubin is the compound that is a component of bile.

text: Order the following three enzymes in chronological order encountered in the digestive tract: 1) Amylase; 2) Trypsin; 3) Pepsin.
explainAnswer: Identify the source of each enzyme: Amylase is produced in the saliva, Pepsin is produced in the stomach, and Trypsin is produced in the pancreas.
Determine the order of digestion: Food enters the mouth first where amylase begins starch digestion.
Next, food moves to the stomach where pepsin starts protein digestion.
Finally, the partially digested food enters the small intestine where trypsin continues protein digestion.

text: Hector finds an animal zygote and during the 4 cell stage removes one of the 4 cells. The resulting cells develop into an adult animal that is missing major organs. Identify all of the following three phyla that this animal could belong to: 1) Echinodermata; 2) Chordata; 3) Nematoda.
explainAnswer: Understand that in the 4 cell stage of development, each cell can contribute to different structures in the organism.
Recognize that Echinodermata and Chordata typically have more complex developmental processes and rely on all cells for proper organ formation.
Identify that Nematoda, being simpler organisms, can sometimes develop normally even if one cell is removed, leading to the possibility of missing organs.

text: Which of the following sources of DNA would be MOST useful for comparing distantly related species of invertebrates?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of DNA or genes listed and their typical uses in genetic comparison.
Understand that mitochondrial DNA is inherited maternally and accumulates mutations at a relatively constant rate.
Recognize that mitochondrial DNA is often used for studying evolutionary relationships over long periods, especially in distantly related species.
Compare this with the other options, which may be more useful for closely related species or specific functions rather than broad evolutionary comparisons.

text: In chickens, dwarfism is a Z-linked recessive disease. What is the probability that a daughter of an unaffected female chicken and an affected male chicken is affected?
explainAnswer: Identify the genotype of the affected male chicken, which is Z^d (where Z^d represents the dwarfism allele).
Determine the genotype of the unaffected female chicken, which is Z^+Z (where Z^+ represents the normal allele).
Cross the genotypes: the affected male can only pass on the Z^d allele, while the unaffected female can pass on either Z^+ or Z.
The possible genotypes for the daughters are Z^+Z^d (unaffected) and Z^dZ (affected).
Since all daughters will inherit the Z^d allele from the affected male, they will all be carriers but not affected, leading to a 100% probability of being unaffected but carriers.

text: In order to oppose the action of the renin angiotensin aldosterone (read:al-DOSS-tuh-rohn) system, the atria of the heart release what hormone to inhibit Na<sup>+</sup> reabsorption?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of the renin angiotensin aldosterone system in regulating sodium reabsorption.
Understand that the heart's atria have a counter-regulatory function to this system.
Recall the specific hormone released by the atria that opposes sodium reabsorption.
Conclude that the hormone released is Atrial Natriuretic Factor.

text: Identify all of the following three behaviors that are found in palatable species: 1) Mullerian mimicry; 2) Batesian (read:BAYT-see-uhn) mimicry; 3) Cryptic coloration.
explainAnswer: Understand that palatable species can exhibit mimicry and coloration for survival.
Recognize that Batesian mimicry involves a palatable species mimicking an unpalatable one for protection.
Identify that cryptic coloration helps palatable species blend into their environment to avoid predation.
Note that Mullerian mimicry involves two unpalatable species resembling each other, which does not apply to palatable species.

text: Brown adipose tissue is responsible for nonshivering thermogenesis. What protein in brown adipose tissue, which serves as a proton leak channel, is responsible for this generation of heat?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of brown adipose tissue, which is to generate heat through nonshivering thermogenesis.
Recognize that the key protein involved in this process is a proton leak channel.
Recall the specific name of the protein that facilitates this function in brown adipose tissue.
Conclude that the protein responsible for nonshivering thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue is thermogenin.

text: Theresia is doing a Gram stain on her sample of bacteria. Assuming she is not decolorizing using ethanol, order the following three reagents in chronological order of administration: 1) Safranin; 2) Crystal violet; 3) Iodine.
explainAnswer: Identify the purpose of each reagent in the Gram staining process.
Recognize that crystal violet is the primary stain applied first to color all bacteria.
Understand that iodine is used as a mordant to fix the crystal violet to the bacterial cells.
Conclude that safranin is the counterstain applied last to color the Gram-negative bacteria after decolorization.

text: Which of the following pairs of amino acids can you NOT distinguish using SDS page?
explainAnswer: Understand that SDS-PAGE separates proteins based on their molecular weight.
Identify the structural similarities between the amino acids in each pair.
Determine which pairs have similar molecular weights and would migrate similarly in SDS-PAGE.
Recognize that leucine and isoleucine have very similar structures and molecular weights, making them indistinguishable by this method.

text: The Magic School Bus is stuck in a plasma B cell! They attach onto a protein marked with a KDEL sequence. Assuming they start in the Golgi, order the following three proteins they will meet from first to last: 1) Chaperonin (read:shap-err-row-nin); 2) COPI (read:COP one); 3) COPII (read:COP two).
explainAnswer: Identify the order of protein transport from the Golgi apparatus.
Recognize that COPII proteins are involved in transporting proteins from the ER to the Golgi, so they will be encountered first.
Understand that COPI proteins mediate retrograde transport from the Golgi back to the ER, so they will be encountered next.
Finally, chaperonins assist in protein folding and will be encountered last as they function within the ER.

text: While the coleoptile (read:koh-lee-OP-tile) covers the plumule (read:PLOOM-yool), the coleorhiza (read:koh-lee-uh-RYE-zuh) is responsible for covering and protecting what structure?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of the coleorhiza in plant development.
Recall that the coleorhiza is a protective sheath in seed germination.
Determine which part of the seed is typically covered by the coleorhiza.
Conclude that the structure covered by the coleorhiza is the radicle.

text: Instead of petals, some plants like euphorbs (read:you-forbes) use what decorative modified leaves associated with flowers to attract pollinators?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of plants mentioned in the question, which are euphorbs.
Recall the purpose of the structures associated with flowers that attract pollinators.
Consider the terminology used in botany for modified leaves that serve this decorative purpose.
Recognize that the correct term for these modified leaves is 'bracts'.

text: Density-dependent inhibition in cancer cells is analogous to what process in bacteria, responsible for regulating biofilm formation?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of density-dependent inhibition in cancer cells, which refers to the regulation of cell growth based on population density.
Consider how bacteria communicate and regulate their behavior based on population density.
Research the process in bacteria that allows them to sense their population density and coordinate behavior, which is known as quorum sensing.
Draw parallels between the regulation of cell growth in cancer cells and the regulation of biofilm formation in bacteria through quorum sensing.

text: Boheng’s chrysanthemum seeds are about to germinate, but midterms are looming. If Boheng wants to delay germination until they get their free time back, identify all of the following three treatments they could apply to the seeds: 1) Abscisic (read: ab-SISS-ik) acid; 2) Far-red light; 3) White light.
explainAnswer: Understand that abscisic acid is a plant hormone that inhibits germination.
Recognize that far-red light can signal to seeds that conditions are not favorable for germination.
Identify that white light typically promotes germination, so it would not be a suitable treatment for delaying germination.
Conclude that the treatments that could delay germination are abscisic acid and far-red light.

text: Which of the following treatments is most likely to yield minimal bacterial growth in the Ames test for mutagenicity?
explainAnswer: Understand that the Ames test is used to assess the mutagenic potential of compounds by measuring bacterial growth.
Identify that Ascorbic Acid is an antioxidant that can reduce oxidative stress and potentially minimize DNA damage.
Consider how the other options, such as Ethidium Bromide and Reactive oxygen species, are likely to increase mutagenicity or bacterial growth.
Evaluate the effects of UV radiation, which can cause DNA damage and increase mutation rates.
Conclude that Ascorbic Acid is the most likely treatment to yield minimal bacterial growth due to its protective antioxidant properties.

text: Kat finds a fish that produces extensive amounts of TMAO in its tissue. Identify all of the following three statements that would likely be true about this fish: 1) It has a lateral line; 2) It has jaws; 3) It is ovoviviparous.
explainAnswer: Identify that TMAO is commonly found in fish that live in deep or extreme environments, which often have adaptations for survival.
Recognize that the presence of a lateral line is a characteristic of many fish species, helping them detect movement and vibrations in the water.
Understand that having jaws is a feature of most modern fish, allowing them to capture prey effectively.
Note that ovoviviparity is a reproductive strategy found in some fish species, where eggs develop inside the female and are born live.
Conclude that all three statements are likely true for a fish producing extensive amounts of TMAO, as they represent common traits in fish adapted to their environments.

text: Dr. Katherine is doing karyotypes of her patients. Which of the following patients’ karyotypes would have a normal number of chromosomes?
choices: A patient with Klinefelter and cri du chat (read:cree-doo-shaa) syndrome
A patient with Klinefelter and Prader-du Willi syndrome
A patient with Turner and Down syndrome
A patient with Turner and Angelmann syndrome
explainAnswer: Identify the normal human chromosome count, which is 46 chromosomes.
Analyze each patient's karyotype to determine the number of chromosomes present.
Klinefelter syndrome typically has 47 chromosomes (XXY), Turner syndrome has 45 (X0), and Down syndrome has 47 (trisomy 21).
Determine that the combination of Turner and Down syndrome results in a total of 45 + 47 = 46 chromosomes, which is normal.
Confirm that the other combinations result in abnormal chromosome counts.

text: Identify all of the following three places where one could find portal systems in the human body: 1) Median eminence of infundibulum (read:in-fun-DIB-yuhlum); 2) Hepatic vein; 3) Circle of willis in the brain.
explainAnswer: Understand what a portal system is, which is a system of blood vessels that carries blood from one capillary bed to another before returning to the heart.
Identify the locations mentioned in the question and determine if they are known to have portal systems.
The median eminence of the infundibulum is part of the hypothalamic-pituitary portal system, which is a true portal system.
The hepatic vein is involved in the hepatic portal system, which carries blood from the gastrointestinal tract to the liver.
The Circle of Willis does not function as a portal system, as it is a network of arteries supplying blood to the brain.

text: Dr. Pujan is treating his patient a Sam with a unique disease where noncoding LINE elements are hyperactive, causing mutagenesis. Knowing this, which of the following noncoding RNAs would be MOST effective in treating Sam?
explainAnswer: Understand that LINE elements are a type of transposable element that can cause mutations.
Recognize that piRNAs are specifically involved in silencing transposable elements and protecting the genome from their activity.
Eliminate other noncoding RNAs based on their functions: miRNAs and siRNAs primarily regulate gene expression, while snRNAs are involved in splicing.
Conclude that piRNAs would be the most effective in treating the hyperactivity of LINE elements due to their role in transposon silencing.

text: A wobble base pair is a pairing between two nucleotides in RNA molecules that does not follow Watson-Crick base pair rules. In tRNA, what nucleobase is present that contributes to three of the four main wobble base pairs?
explainAnswer: Understand that wobble base pairs occur in tRNA and involve non-standard pairing between nucleotides.
Recall the structure of tRNA and the nucleobases it contains, including adenine, cytosine, guanine, uracil, and hypoxanthine.
Identify that hypoxanthine is a modified nucleobase derived from adenine that can pair with multiple bases.
Recognize that hypoxanthine contributes to three of the four main wobble base pairs in tRNA.

text: Tyrosinase (read:tie-RAH-sin-ase) is lacking in individuals with what disorder which is characterized by a lack of melanin production in keratinocytes (read: kerr-uh-TEE-noh-sights)?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of tyrosinase in melanin production.
Understand that a deficiency in tyrosinase leads to reduced melanin.
Recognize that the disorder characterized by a lack of melanin production is albinism.
Connect the absence of tyrosinase to the symptoms of albinism.

text: Stimulated emission depletion microscopy is a novel microscopy technique which utilizes selective deactivation of neighboring fluorophores to narrow down their effective fluorescence spot and overcome the diffraction limit. This is similar to the function of what group of cells in the eye?
explainAnswer: Understand that the question is asking for a comparison between a microscopy technique and a specific group of cells in the eye.
Recall the function of horizontal cells in the retina, which help in processing visual information by integrating signals from photoreceptors.
Recognize that horizontal cells play a role in enhancing contrast and spatial resolution, similar to how stimulated emission depletion microscopy enhances resolution.

Eliminate other options by considering their primary functions: rods are for low-light vision, ganglion cells transmit visual information to the brain, and bipolar cells connect photoreceptors to ganglion cells.
Conclude that horizontal cells are the best analogy for the function described in the microscopy technique.

text: Most strains of syphillis are resistant to 50S inhibiting antibiotics such as macrolides because they contain mutations in what enzyme found in the large ribosomal subunit that catalyzes the formation of peptide bonds?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of the 50S ribosomal subunit in protein synthesis.
Understand that peptidyl transferase is an enzyme that catalyzes peptide bond formation.
Recognize that mutations in the enzyme can lead to antibiotic resistance.
Conclude that the correct answer is the enzyme affected by these mutations.

text: A population initially in Hardy-Weinberg equillibrium is fixed at a locus, until one individual introduces a mutant allele. Given that the allele is highly beneficial, and inherited autosomal recessively, which of the following best describes how the frequency of the new mutant allele will change?
choices: Increasing rapidly at first, then slowly until fixation
Increasing slowly at first, then rapidly until fixation
Increasing slowly at first, then decreasing until equillibrium
explainAnswer: Recognize that the introduction of a beneficial mutant allele in a population can change allele frequencies over time.
Understand that since the allele is inherited autosomal recessively, it will initially be present in low frequency and may take time to increase.
Consider that the beneficial nature of the allele will lead to a gradual increase in frequency as more individuals carrying the allele reproduce.
Realize that once the allele reaches a certain frequency, its advantage will cause a rapid increase until it becomes fixed in the population.
Conclude that the best description of this process is 'Increasing slowly at first, then rapidly until fixation.'

text: Larry is studying fragile X syndrome, which follows an X-linked dominant inheritance that gets worse every generation. Which of the following causes could explain why this is true?
explainAnswer: Understand that fragile X syndrome is caused by genetic mutations that can expand in successive generations.
Recognize that trinucleotide repeat expansions are known to increase in number with each generation, leading to more severe symptoms.
Eliminate other options by noting that hypermethylation, loss of function inversions, and gain of function insertions do not typically result in generational worsening of symptoms.
Conclude that trinucleotide repeat expansion is the most plausible explanation for the worsening of fragile X syndrome across generations.

text: In the evolution of vertebrates, order the following three traits by the order in which they evolved: 1) Amniotic egg; 2) Mineralized skeleton; 3) Limbs with digits.
explainAnswer: Identify the evolutionary timeline of vertebrates and the traits in question.
Research the first appearance of each trait in the fossil record.
Determine that mineralized skeletons appeared first, followed by limbs with digits, and finally the amniotic egg.
Order the traits based on their first appearance in evolutionary history.

text: A patient suffers a localized stroke that destroys their entire thalamus. Which of the following senses would be LEAST affected?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of the thalamus in sensory processing, noting that it acts as a relay station for most sensory information except for smell.
Recognize that olfaction (smell) bypasses the thalamus and goes directly to the olfactory bulb and cortex.
Evaluate the other senses: vision, audition (hearing), and gustation (taste), which all rely on thalamic processing.
Conclude that since olfaction does not depend on the thalamus, it would be the least affected by its destruction.

text: Hybridomas (read:high-bruh-DOH-muhs) are a type of synthetic tumor used to produce monoclonal antibodies. They are made by fusing immortal myeloma cells with what immune cell type?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of cells involved in the production of monoclonal antibodies.
Recognize that hybridomas are created by fusing two different types of cells.
Determine that one of the cells is an immortal myeloma cell.
Recall that the other cell type involved in antibody production is a B cell.
Conclude that the correct answer is B cell.

text: Order the following three portions of the cytoskeleton (read: caito-skeleton) in increasing radius of the fiber: 1) Intermediate filaments; 2) Microtubules (read: Micro-tu-biuls); 3) Microfilaments.
explainAnswer: Identify the three components of the cytoskeleton: microfilaments, intermediate filaments, and microtubules.
Recall that microfilaments are the thinnest, followed by intermediate filaments, and then microtubules, which are the thickest.
Order the components based on their thickness from smallest to largest: microfilaments (3), intermediate filaments (1), and microtubules (2).
Write the final order as 312.

text: ABC transporters are ATP dependant pumps that export compounds from the cell against their concentration gradients. Identify all of the following three ions in a human cell that ABC transporters would possibly export: 1) Na<sup>+</sup> (read:sodium plus); 2) K<sup>+</sup> (read:potassium plus); 3) Cl<sup>-</sup> (read:chlorine).
explainAnswer: Understand that ABC transporters are primarily involved in exporting substances against their concentration gradients using ATP.
Recognize that sodium (Na<sup>+</sup>) and chloride (Cl<sup>-</sup>) ions are often found in higher concentrations outside the cell compared to inside, making them candidates for export.
Note that potassium (K<sup>+</sup>) typically has a higher concentration inside the cell, so it is less likely to be exported by ABC transporters.
Conclude that ABC transporters would likely export Na<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>-</sup> from the cell, but not K<sup>+</sup> due to its concentration gradient.

text: Aryan is studying a certain plant. He is trying to figure out what must be true about the plant if it stores malic acid at night in it’s central vacuole. Which of the following statements MUST also be true of this plant?
choices: It opens it’s stomata (read:stO-mata) during the day
explainAnswer: Identify that storing malic acid at night indicates the plant likely uses a specific type of photosynthesis called CAM (Crassulacean Acid Metabolism).
Recognize that CAM plants typically utilize PEP carboxylase to fix carbon dioxide at night, converting it into malic acid.
Eliminate the other options by noting that halophytes, significant photorespiration, and daytime stomatal opening do not directly relate to the storage of malic acid at night.
Conclude that since the plant stores malic acid at night, it must utilize PEP carboxylase.

text: Which of the following environmental pressures most strongly favors the evolution of intercalary (read:inter-Kalary) meristems in a plant?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of intercalary meristems in plant growth, which is to allow for regrowth after damage.
Consider the environmental pressures listed and how they affect plant survival and growth.
Evaluate how grazing by herbivores directly damages plant tissues, necessitating rapid regrowth.
Compare this with the other pressures, noting that they do not directly cause tissue loss in the same way.
Conclude that grazing by herbivores is the strongest pressure favoring the evolution of intercalary meristems.

text: Jason is trying to manually insert aquaporins into the wall of the collecting duct of a mammalian kidney. The same effect is triggered by what posterior pituitary (read:pitu-a-tery) hormone?
explainAnswer: Identify the function of aquaporins in the kidney, which is to facilitate water reabsorption.
Recall that the posterior pituitary releases hormones that regulate kidney function.
Recognize that the hormone responsible for increasing aquaporin insertion in the collecting duct is ADH (antidiuretic hormone).
Conclude that the effect of inserting aquaporins is mimicked by the action of ADH.

text: Caleb is studying cells with MHC class one. Which of the following cells could he NOT be studying?
explainAnswer: Understand that MHC class I molecules are present on the surface of most nucleated cells.
Identify which of the given cell types are nucleated and which are not.
Recognize that red blood cells do not have a nucleus and therefore do not express MHC class I.
Eliminate the other cell types (platelets, dendritic cells, astrocytes) as they are all nucleated and can express MHC class I.

text: Identify all of the following three blood types that are NOT possible for a child of two parents with blood types A and B: 1) O type; 2) A type; 3) B type
explainAnswer: Determine the possible genotypes for parents with blood types A and B, which can be AA, AO, BB, or BO.
List the possible blood types for their children based on the combinations of these genotypes.
Recognize that the child can inherit A or O from the A parent and B or O from the B parent.
Conclude that the possible blood types for the child are A, B, AB, and O.
Since all listed blood types (O, A, B) are possible, the answer is NONE.

text: Which of the following amino acids could best replace tyrosine (read:tairo-sin) on receptor tyrosine kinases (read:kina-ses)?
explainAnswer: Identify the functional groups and properties of tyrosine, which has a hydroxyl group and is polar.
Examine the properties of each amino acid in the choices to find one that is also polar and can mimic tyrosine's function.
Determine that serine has a hydroxyl group similar to tyrosine, making it a suitable replacement.
Eliminate alanine and proline as they are non-polar, and phenylalanine as it lacks the hydroxyl group.

text: What general phenomenon, which occurs when cells fail to undergo cytokinesis, is lethal in most animal cells but a common trait in plants?
explainAnswer: Identify the process of cytokinesis and its role in cell division.
Understand the consequences of failed cytokinesis in animal cells, leading to lethality.
Research how plants can tolerate or even benefit from polyploidy.
Recognize that polyploidy is the condition of having more than two complete sets of chromosomes, which is common in plants.

text: After her bunny spins, Selena gives him a carrot. What type of operant conditioning is this?
explainAnswer: Identify the behavior being reinforced, which is the bunny spinning.
Determine the consequence that follows the behavior, which is giving a carrot.
Recognize that giving a carrot is adding a positive stimulus.
Conclude that this is an example of positive reinforcement, as it encourages the behavior to occur again.

text: Which of the following is most likely true about the first enzymes on earth?
choices: They were composed of amino acid subunits
They were similar in structure to most current enzymes
They required other macromolecules for replication
explainAnswer: Consider the basic building blocks of enzymes and their structures.
Identify that the earliest enzymes would likely be simpler and not necessarily composed of amino acids.
Recognize that phosphodiester bonds are characteristic of nucleic acids, which may have been among the first biological molecules.
Eliminate options that suggest complexity or reliance on other macromolecules for replication.

text: Order the following three blood vessels from first to last in terms of distance needed to reach them from the right ventricle: 1) Pulmonary vein; 2) Pulmonary artery; 3) Hepatic portal vein
explainAnswer: Identify the path of blood flow starting from the right ventricle.
Recognize that the pulmonary artery carries blood to the lungs, making it the first vessel encountered.
Understand that the pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart, making them the second vessel.
Note that the hepatic portal vein carries blood from the digestive organs to the liver, which is further away, making it the last vessel.

text: Dideoxynucleotide (read:di-dee-oxy-NEW-clee-oh-tide) triphosphates, used for Sanger Sequencing, lack what functional group at the 3’ carbon necessary for DNA elongation?
