explainAnswer: Identify the structure of a nucleotide and its components, including the sugar, phosphate groups, and nitrogenous base.
Focus on the sugar component, which is deoxyribose in DNA nucleotides.
Examine the 3' carbon of the sugar and determine what functional group is typically present for DNA elongation.
Recognize that dideoxynucleotides lack the hydroxyl (-OH) group at the 3' carbon, which is essential for forming phosphodiester bonds during DNA synthesis.

text: Which of the following fungal divisions have the highest proportion of organisms that form arbuscular mycorrhizae (read:ar-BUS-kew-lar mai-koh-RIHzae)?
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristic of arbuscular mycorrhizae, which is their association with plant roots.
Recognize that Glomeromycota is the division known for forming arbuscular mycorrhizae.
Eliminate other divisions by noting that they do not predominantly form this type of mycorrhizae.
Confirm that Glomeromycota has the highest proportion of organisms that form arbuscular mycorrhizae.

text: Mollusks are able to mechanically breakdown food before it enters their digestive tract through what teeth like feeding structure?
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics of mollusks and their feeding mechanisms.
Research the anatomical structures involved in the feeding process of mollusks.
Look for specific terms associated with the feeding structures of mollusks.
Confirm that the term 'radula' refers to the teeth-like structure used for mechanical breakdown of food.

text: Select all of the following four hormones in the female reproductive system whose level rises during the luteal phase after ovulation in a nonpregant person. 1) LH; 2) FSH; 3) Estrogen; 4) Progesterone
explainAnswer: Understand the phases of the menstrual cycle, focusing on the luteal phase which follows ovulation.
Identify the hormones that are primarily involved in the luteal phase, particularly those produced by the corpus luteum.
Recognize that progesterone levels rise significantly during the luteal phase to prepare the uterus for potential implantation.
Note that estrogen levels also increase during the luteal phase, although not as prominently as progesterone.
Eliminate LH and FSH as they peak during ovulation and decrease afterwards, confirming that only estrogen and progesterone levels rise.

text: Aryan is studying germ layers and tries to identify them in Cnidarians (read:nai-DAR-ee-uhnz). Identify all of the following three germ layers that can be found in all cnidarians: 1) Ectoderm; 2) Endoderm; 3) Mesoderm.
explainAnswer: Understand that cnidarians are diploblastic organisms, meaning they have two primary germ layers.
Identify the two germ layers in cnidarians: ectoderm and endoderm.
Recognize that cnidarians do not possess a mesoderm, which is the third germ layer found in triploblastic organisms.
Conclude that the correct germ layers present in all cnidarians are ectoderm and endoderm.

text: If Aryan has constituitively active G protein coupled receptors, the signaling pathway of which of the following tastes is least likely to be affected?
explainAnswer: Identify the role of G protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) in taste signaling.
Understand that sour taste primarily relies on ion channels rather than GPCRs.
Recognize that bitter, umami, and sweet tastes are all mediated by GPCRs.
Conclude that since sour taste is least dependent on GPCRs, it is least likely to be affected by constitutively active GPCRs.

text: Rank the following three cells by increasing size of their rough ER: 1) B cell; 2) Erythrocyte; 3) T cell.
explainAnswer: Understand that rough ER is involved in protein synthesis and is typically more abundant in cells that produce a lot of proteins.
Recognize that B cells are involved in antibody production, which requires significant amounts of rough ER.
Note that T cells also produce proteins but generally less than B cells, while erythrocytes do not have rough ER as they lose their organelles during maturation.
Rank the cells based on their rough ER abundance: erythrocytes have none, T cells have some, and B cells have the most.

text: Identify all of the following three groups of algae that have sporopollenin: 1) Green algae; 2) Brown algae; 3) Red algae;
explainAnswer: Understand that sporopollenin is a tough biopolymer found in the walls of spores and pollen grains.
Research the characteristics of each group of algae to determine the presence of sporopollenin.
Identify that only green algae are known to have sporopollenin in their reproductive structures.
Conclude that brown and red algae do not possess sporopollenin.

text: Choanoflagellates (read:koh-ANN-oh-fla-gel-ates) are considered the sister group to animals because they resemble the feeding cells of what animal phylum?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of choanoflagellates and their similarities to animal cells.
Recall the animal phyla that have feeding cells, particularly focusing on those that are simple and primitive.
Recognize that Porifera, commonly known as sponges, possess feeding cells called choanocytes that resemble choanoflagellates.
Conclude that Porifera is the correct phylum related to choanoflagellates based on their structural similarities.

text: Derek is isolating in vivo dog chromosomes, but he finds that there is a double strand break. Identify all of the following three biological repair mechanisms that are able to repair double strand breaks: 1) Nucleotide excision repair; 2) Base excision repair; 3) Mismatch repair.
explainAnswer: Understand that double strand breaks are a specific type of DNA damage that requires specialized repair mechanisms.
Recognize that nucleotide excision repair, base excision repair, and mismatch repair are primarily used for single strand breaks and other types of DNA damage.
Identify the correct repair mechanisms for double strand breaks, which include homologous recombination and non-homologous end joining, not the ones listed.

text: During fertilization, the cortical reaction is triggered by the entry of what ion into the egg?
explainAnswer: Identify the process of fertilization and its key events.
Understand the role of the cortical reaction in preventing polyspermy.
Recognize that the entry of specific ions triggers the cortical reaction.
Recall that calcium ions (Ca2+) are known to play a crucial role in this process.
Conclude that the ion responsible for triggering the cortical reaction is Ca2+.

text: Yunyi has overwatered his bean plant. To form an airway for the submerged roots, the bean plant sends a death signal to cells in the root cortex. It does this using what hormone?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which involves plant biology and hormone functions.
Recall the role of hormones in plants, particularly in response to stress or damage.
Consider the specific scenario of overwatering and how plants typically respond to such conditions.
Recognize that ethylene is a hormone associated with stress responses, including signaling for cell death in roots.
Conclude that the hormone responsible for sending a death signal in this scenario is ethylene.

text: Heartwood and sapwood in woody plants make up what tissue layer that forms interior to the vascular cambium?
answer: SECONDARY XYLEM (DO NOT ACCEPT: PRIMARY XYLEM)
explainAnswer: Identify the layers of tissue in woody plants, focusing on the vascular cambium.
Understand that the vascular cambium is responsible for producing secondary tissues.
Recognize that heartwood and sapwood are both types of secondary xylem.
Conclude that the tissue layer formed interior to the vascular cambium is called secondary xylem.

text: Rank the following three phyla of organisms by most related to least related to humans: 1) Nematoda; 2) Platyhelminthes (read:pla-tee-hel-minth-ees); 3) Echinodermata (read:ee-k.ai-no-der-mah-ta)
explainAnswer: Identify the evolutionary relationships among the phyla based on their common ancestors.
Determine that Echinodermata and humans share a more recent common ancestor compared to Nematoda and Platyhelminthes.
Rank Echinodermata as most related to humans, followed by Nematoda, and then Platyhelminthes as least related.
